title: Compile generated libyaml crate

Regenerate the crate with the required libyaml include/version SLATE_CLANG_ARGS, fix each child root cause, and file new children only for new cargo check failures that appear after these are resolved. title: Add library-mode project translation CLI
description: Objective: make Slate run against the libyaml library sources cloned at ~/libyaml. Add a library-mode project translation CLI path for C projects without a main translation unit, so libyaml can be translated as a library rooted at lib.rs instead of failing because translate-project requires main. title: Lower generic CIR scalar op spellings
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.binop and cir.unary as P0 unsupported generic scalar spellings that can block ordinary C emitted by newer/different CIR producers.

What to do:
- Add parsing/lowering for cir.binop and cir.unary spellings.
- Reuse existing scalar arithmetic, bitwise, logical, and unary lowering semantics where possible.
- Add differential fixtures that force these spellings.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md when the ops are supported.
close_reason: cir.binop/cir.unary are incubator-only generic spellings; upstream ClangIR (our producer) emits split named ops (cir.add, cir.minus, ...) instead and never emits these, so they can't be differentially tested. Not implementing. Documented in docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.

title: Lower low-level CIR branch variants
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.brcond and cir.switch.flat as P0 unsupported control-flow variants. Slate supports structured branch/switch forms, but these lower-level forms can appear and should not block ordinary C.

What to do:
- Add parser and lowerer support for cir.brcond.
- Add parser and lowerer support for cir.switch.flat.
- Prefer structured Rust output when the CFG shape permits it; use conservative state-machine style only when needed.
- Add differential fixtures and update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: cir.brcond/cir.switch.flat come only from --cir-flatten-cfg, which Slate never runs. Verified: if/else, ternary, &&, ||, for, while, do-while, switch, goto all stay structured through Slate's emit pipeline (0 brcond/switch.flat). Supporting them would be untestable dead code. Documented in docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.

title: Keep ptr_len scalar extent params unless removable
description: Pointer-to-slice lifting currently deletes/materializes scalar length parameters whenever they are used as a proven pointer extent. That is too aggressive: length remains part of the C function API and must stay as a parameter when it is explicitly passed, while pointer params can still lift to slices. Also constant-bound loops over proven array-backed pointers should allow pointer-to-slice/index recovery even without a scalar length parameter.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix ptr_len array-to-slice provenance (soundness + interprocedural)
description:
src/fixups/facts/ptr_len.rs currently promotes (pointer,length) parameter pairs to safe slices based on coincidence, not provenance: adjacent_ptr_len_pair only considers the first adjacent (ptr,int) param pair, collect_body_arrays flattens array lengths by raw name across scopes (scope leakage), and callsite() only checks that the length argument's literal value happens to equal the array's length rather than proving dataflow identity. This means it can pick the wrong pair, cross-match shadowed arrays of the same length, and can never prove a pointer/length pair that is forwarded unchanged through a chain of function calls.

Rework around a whole-program fixed-point analysis (same pattern as facts/string_params.rs's char*->&str lift): BindingId-keyed candidate pairs, a LengthSource::{Const(u64) from real array type, Bound(BindingId) from an active candidate's own param} provenance model, and per-callsite dataflow proof instead of literal-value coincidence. Adds interprocedural propagation so forwarded ptr/len pairs across function-call boundaries can also be proven and converted to real &[T]/&mut [T] slices. Full design in /home/takashi/.claude/plans/fluffy-weaving-bengio.md.
acceptance_criteria: adjacent_ptr_len_pair considers all adjacent pairs, not just the first; array length provenance is BindingId-scoped (no name-based scope leakage); callsite matching is a genuine identity proof (const array length or forwarded-binding identity), not literal-value coincidence; a ptr/len pair forwarded unchanged through a chain of function calls (outer(p,n){inner(p,n);}) is provably convertible to a slice; new unit tests cover direct-case regressions, interprocedural forwarding, shadowed-array negative case, multi-pair negative case, coincidental-literal negative case, and reassigned-param negative case; cargo fmt && cargo nextest r --release passes
notes: touches: src/fixups/facts/ptr_len.rs, ptr_len fixup tests/fixtures
close_reason: Implemented binding/provenance-based ptr_len slice lifting: candidate pointer/integer pairs now require callee-side extent use or unchanged forwarding, preserve unrelated printable parameters, support non-adjacent extent parameters, and added ptr_len_nonadjacent differential coverage. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, and cargo nextest r --release.

close_reason: Emit typedef'd anonymous records (yaml_string_t) via typedef-name adoption in c_ast, and function-local anonymous structs (anon.N STACK/QUEUE locals) synthesized from CIR type-alias layout + get_member field names, emitted per-module. libyaml crate 'cannot find type' errors: 58 -> 0. Remaining crate errors are unrelated signedness/field mismatches.

title: Fix typed dispatch-loop break mismatch in generated libyaml output
description: cargo check of the generated ~/libyaml crate reports E0308 mismatched types for labeled dispatch-loop breaks such as break '__dispatch0; in contexts expecting i32. Representative locations from /tmp/slate-libyaml-crate include src/api.rs:1424, src/api.rs:2482, src/api.rs:2787, src/api.rs:2928, and src/api.rs:3091. Emit a value-carrying break or restructure the state-machine lowering so typed contexts compile.
notes: Fixed in src/lower.rs lower_dispatch: value-returning functions put the dispatch loop in tail position, so the wildcard 'break $dispatch (yielding ()) mismatched the return type (E0308). Reaching the wildcard = C ran off the end of a non-void function (UB), so it now emits unreachable!(), making the loop diverge (!) and coerce to the return type. Void functions keep break (already correct). Added fixture tests/fixtures/goto_return_value.c; 211 tests pass. Regenerated ~/libyaml crate: 0 dispatch-break errors remain (only E0425 from q0g.1).
close_reason: Dispatch-loop break mismatch fixed: value-returning functions emit unreachable!() at the wildcard so the loop diverges and coerces to the return type; verified in isolation and on regenerated libyaml crate (no E0308 dispatch errors).

title: Lower CIR aggregate extract and insert member ops
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.extract_member and cir.insert_member as P1 unsupported. Aggregate value mutation/extraction appears once structs/unions are manipulated by value rather than only through addresses.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for cir.extract_member and cir.insert_member.
- Preserve C aggregate semantics while generating Rust field/member updates compatible with existing struct representation.
- Add differential fixtures for struct value extraction, mutation, nested aggregates, and array-containing structs where supported.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Implemented cir.extract_member/cir.insert_member lowering for struct values, added synthetic lowerer tests for both op spellings, added aggregate_value_member_ops differential fixture for by-value aggregate coverage, and updated docs/cir-op-prioritization.md. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo fmt, cargo run -- emit-fixtures, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Lower CIR memory operation intrinsics
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.libc.memchr, cir.libc.memcpy, cir.libc.memmove, cir.libc.memset, cir.memcpy_inline, and cir.memset_inline as P1 unsupported. Memory operations are high-leverage for real C and stdlib expansion.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for the CIR memory operation family.
- Map libc and inline forms to Rust/libc/std::ptr operations with correct overlap behavior for memmove versus memcpy.
- Add differential fixtures for scalar buffers, struct/array copies, memset zero/nonzero, memchr hits/misses, and overlapping memmove.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Lowered the cir.libc.mem* family (memcpy/memmove/memset/memchr) to byte-wise std::ptr ops + __slate_memchr helper; added PtrCopy/WriteBytes AST nodes and 4 differential fixtures. Plain libc mem* calls already worked via extern; only clang builtins/aggregate bit_cast raise these ops. Idiom-recognizer is a no-op stub upstream (noted in emit.rs).

title: Lower CIR bitfield get and set ops
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.get_bitfield and cir.set_bitfield as P1 unsupported. C bitfields are common in systems headers and data layouts.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for cir.get_bitfield and cir.set_bitfield.
- Preserve signedness, width, offset, masking, and update semantics from CIR.
- Add differential fixtures for signed/unsigned bitfields, adjacent fields, boundary widths, and read-modify-write updates.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Lowered cir.get_bitfield/cir.set_bitfield as mask+sign-extend over per-field struct storage (behaviorally identical to CIR shared storage for well-defined C). Added bitfield_ops differential fixture (signed/unsigned, adjacent fields, boundary widths, read-modify-write, 40-bit long-long) and marked ops supported in docs. Verified: cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release (116 passed).

title: Lower CIR decrement op
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.dec as P1 unsupported while cir.inc is supported. Decrement is common in loops and pointer/index code.

What to do:

title: Lower CIR atomics to real Rust atomics (AtomicN::from_ptr)
description: Replace the non-atomic RMW lowering of cir.atomic.* with genuine std::sync::atomic ops so the output is correct once multithreaded programs land. Use AtomicN::from_ptr(store_address(ptr)) to view the existing integer slot atomically without changing its storage. fetch->fetch_add/sub/and/or/xor/nand/max/min (recompute new value when fetch_first is absent); xchg->swap; cmpxchg->compare_exchange (strong, to stay deterministic); fence->std::sync::atomic::fence. Also route mem_order-carrying cir.load/cir.store to atomic load()/store() so a shared _Atomic object is never accessed non-atomically (else data race under threads). Float/pointer atomics keep the non-atomic fallback (no std atomic float).
design: atomic_wrapper(rust_ty)->Option<AtomicN name> for i8..u64/isize/usize/bool. Ordering from C mem_order enum (0 relaxed,1 consume,2 acquire,3 release,4 acqrel,5 seqcst); clamp to load/store-valid orderings; consume->Acquire; relaxed thread fence is a no-op (fence(Relaxed) panics in Rust). compare_exchange always strong (weak may spuriously fail and diverge from C in differential tests).
acceptance_criteria: tests/fixtures/atomics.c still passes generated_differential; generated Rust uses AtomicN::from_ptr(...).fetch_*/swap/compare_exchange and atomic load/store; no non-atomic access to _Atomic objects.
close_reason: Atomics now lower to real std::sync::atomic ops via AtomicN::from_ptr (fetch_*/swap/compare_exchange/fence + atomic load/store). atomics.c differential passes; pthread program lowers correct atomic ops. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.fence (thread fence)
description: Lower cir.atomic.fence to std::sync::atomic::fence(Ordering::SeqCst) — a harmless no-op single-threaded. No operands, no result; the ordering attr can be ignored (SeqCst is always safe/strongest).
acceptance_criteria: atomic_thread_fence fixture translates without warnings and passes differential.
close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.cmpxchg (compare-exchange)
description: Lower cir.atomic.cmpxchg(ptr,expected,desired) -> (old, bool). Two results: old = *ptr; ok = old == expected; if ok { *ptr = desired }. Bind result[0]->old (int), result[1]->ok (bool). Surrounding CIR handles writing the actual value back to the C 'expected' lvalue on failure.
acceptance_criteria: atomic_compare_exchange_strong fixture (both success and failure paths) translates without warnings and passes differential.
close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.xchg (atomic exchange)
description: Lower cir.atomic.xchg(ptr,val) -> old: read *store_address(ptr) into a temp, store val, bind result to the old value.
acceptance_criteria: atomic_exchange fixture translates without warnings and passes differential.
close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.fetch (atomic RMW fetch ops)
description: Lower cir.atomic.fetch(ptr,val) to a non-atomic read-modify-write. binop attr selects the op (0=Add,1=Sub,2=And,3=Xor,4=Or,5=Nand,6=Max,7=Min); Nand => !(old & val); Max/Min => old.max/min(val). The fetch_first unit attr means the op returns the pre-op value (fetch_add); its absence means it returns the post-op value (add_fetch). Emit: read *store_address(ptr), compute new, write back, bind result to old or new.
acceptance_criteria: atomic_fetch_add/sub/and/or/xor and __atomic_add_fetch fixtures translate without warnings and pass differential.
close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Support CIR C atomics (cir.atomic.*)
description: C11/GNU atomics lower to distinct CIR ops that Slate currently drops (warns 'unsupported CIR op'): cir.atomic.fetch, cir.atomic.xchg, cir.atomic.cmpxchg, cir.atomic.fence. Atomic loads/stores already lower correctly (plain cir.load/cir.store carrying mem_order/sync_scope attrs, which are safely ignored). Because Slate's correctness bar is single-threaded differential testing, lower these as plain non-atomic read-modify-write through store_address(ptr) (transliterate-first); real Rust atomics are a later idiomatization fixup.
design: Use store_address(ptr) to obtain a uniform *mut T for slot/global/member/element/raw-ptr, then RMW inside unsafe. binop enum: 0=Add,1=Sub,2=And,3=Xor,4=Or,5=Nand,6=Max,7=Min. fetch_first attr present => op returns old value; absent => returns new value.
acceptance_criteria: A C fixture using atomic_fetch_add/sub/and/or/xor, atomic_exchange, atomic_compare_exchange_strong, and atomic_thread_fence translates with no 'unsupported CIR op' warnings and passes generated_differential (identical stdout+exit).
close_reason: All four child ops (fetch/xchg/cmpxchg/fence) lowered and verified via tests/fixtures/atomics.c differential test.

title: Support CIR do-while op cir.do
description: Slate currently emits todo for cir.do. Add a focused C fixture for do-while control flow, inspect CIR shape, implement lowering in src/lower.rs, and verify with differential testing including at least one body-before-condition case.
notes: touches: src/lower.rs, tests/fixtures/do_while.c, tests/support/cgen.rs if fuzz generator coverage is extended
close_reason: Implemented cir.do lowering in src/lower.rs with a focused tests/fixtures/do_while.c fixture covering body-before-condition and continue-to-condition semantics. Verified with cargo test --test differential generated_differential -- --nocapture, cargo nextest r --release, cargo run -- emit-fixtures, generic-c warning scan, and cargo fmt && cargo test after merge.

title: Support CIR arithmetic overflow ops
description: Slate currently emits todo for arithmetic overflow CIR ops such as cir.mul.overflow. Cover the arithmetic overflow family that Clang emits, including add/sub/mul/div/rem or the generic binop.overflow spelling as applicable. Add focused C fixtures, lower according to emitted CIR semantics, and verify with differential testing.
close_reason: Implemented CIR add/sub/mul/div/rem overflow lowering to Rust overflowing_* tuple results and added overflow_scalar_ops differential fixture. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Support CIR decrement op cir.dec
description: Slate currently emits todo for cir.dec. Add a focused C fixture that produces cir.dec, inspect CIR, lower it preserving C pre/post-decrement semantics as emitted by CIR, and verify with differential testing.
close_reason: Implemented cir.dec lowering via the shared inc/dec step helper in src/lower.rs and added tests/fixtures/decrement.c for pre/post-decrement plus unsigned wrap. Verified with cargo test --test differential generated_differential -- --nocapture and cargo fmt && cargo nextest r --release before and after merge.

title: Lower cir.if / conditional control flow (if/else, ternary control)
description: Conditional control flow lowers to a cir.if op slate does not handle -> todo!("cir.if"). Surfaced by misc/assert (assert() expands to an if guarding __assert_fail) but is a fundamental gap (docs list if/switch/break/continue/goto as unhandled). Lower cir.if to Rust if/else.
acceptance_criteria: a fixture using if/else translates, compiles, and matches C; stdlib_coverage misc/assert progresses past the cir.if todo
close_reason: Lowered cir.if to Rust if/else (incl. else-if chains and no-else); added conditionals.c fixture, extended cgen generator + c.bnf + docs; differential, 300-case fuzz, and full suite pass. misc/assert now lowers past the cir.if todo (remaining failure is __assert_fail/puts under slate-4t0).

title: Lower calls to external libc functions via extern "C" declarations
description: Slate emits bare Rust calls to external C symbols (e.g. puts(...), strcpy(...), sqrt(...), malloc(...)) with no declaration, so the generated Rust fails to compile (cannot find function). Only printf is special-cased through libc::printf. Root cause for ~45 of 53 failing stdlib_coverage probes (stdio, string, stdlib, math, ctype helpers). Fix: for any called function with no body in the translation unit, emit an extern "C" { fn name(args) -> ret; } declaration (or route to libc::) so the call links against the system C library. Covers stdlib_coverage probes: stdio/{puts,putchar,fputs,fprintf,sprintf,snprintf}, string/*, stdlib/{atoi,atol,labs,strtol,malloc_free,calloc,qsort}, math/*, ctype/* (via __ctype_b_loc/__ctype_toupper_loc).
acceptance_criteria: stdlib_coverage probes for puts, strcpy, strlen, sqrt, atoi, malloc_free translate, compile, and match C stdout+exit; remove them from KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED
close_reason: Collect body-less cir.func decls into an 'unsafe extern "C"{}' block; extern call sites wrap in unsafe and 'as'-cast fixed args to declared param types (variadic '...' preserved). Also: string literals render *mut (weaken to *const for printf), #cir.ptr<null> -> null_mut(), added cir.ptr_diff (offset_from), and -lm in the C harness. stdlib_coverage 25->40 passing: acceptance probes puts/strcpy/strlen/sqrt/atoi/malloc_free all pass, plus ctype/* (via __ctype_b_loc), libm sqrt/sin/cos/exp/log/pow/fmod, string mem*/str* (chr/rchr/str/cmp/ncmp), atol/calloc/strtol, snprintf/sprintf/putchar. Remaining fails belong to other beads (slate-kaf builtins, slate-61j FILE, slate-aeo div_t, slate-6c2 cir.copy).

title: Refactor fuzz generator into C-subset program generator
description: The current BNF expander mostly stitches fixed template fragments together, so generated programs do not exercise variable scope, expression composition, reusable declarations, or realistic statement interactions. Refactor fuzzing around a C-aware program generator that can consume a grammar/BNF for the supported syntax but also maintain generation state: declared variables, types, scopes, functions, globals, and expression contexts. The generator should produce valid C programs for Slate's supported subset, with variables that can be declared, assigned, read, passed to functions, used in array indices, struct/union fields, loops, sizeof, volatile/static contexts where supported, and combined into expressions/statements without violating C validity. The design should be closer to a small csmith-style generator for our subset than a pure random text expander. It should keep deterministic seeds, shrinking/debuggability where practical, and integrate with the existing differential test harness and BNF fuzz entry point. Acceptance criteria: design is documented; generator can emit multi-function programs with scoped variables and expressions; generated programs compile as C and translate with Slate; differential tests run multiple seeds; existing simple BNF tests are either preserved as smoke tests or migrated cleanly.
notes: Refactoring tests/bnf_fuzz.rs fuzzing around a stateful C-subset generator (tests/support/cgen.rs). Keeps BNF grammar+expander as a smoke test; new generator_differential runs multiple seeds. Value-bound tracking guarantees no i32 overflow / OOB so C==Rust.
close_reason: Refactored fuzzing around a stateful C-subset generator (tests/support/cgen.rs): scope/type env + function-signature state compose multi-function programs with scoped vars, expressions, calls; value-bound tracking guarantees no UB so C==Rust. BNF expander kept as bnf_expander_smoke; generator_differential runs N seeds (40 verified green). Design in docs/fuzzing.md. All tests + fmt pass.

title: Add while loop support
description: Translate simple C while loops from CIR and verify with differential fixtures and BNF fuzz coverage.
close_reason: Implemented simple while-loop lowering by handling cir.while as a conservative Rust loop with a condition-region break, added while_loop.c differential coverage, extended BNF fuzz coverage, and updated docs. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo run --quiet -- emit-fixtures, cargo test -- --nocapture, and git diff --check.

title: Add file-scope static integer globals
description: Translate file-scope static int globals with constant initializers and basic load/store access.
close_reason: Implemented file-scope static int globals by collecting integer cir.global definitions, emitting Rust static mut items, and lowering get_global loads/stores to unsafe static access. Added static_globals.c fixture, generated-Rust shape assertion, BNF fuzz coverage, and docs. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo run --quiet -- emit-fixtures, cargo test -- --nocapture, and git diff --check.

title: Add volatile load/store support
description: Translate CIR volatile loads and stores with Rust volatile pointer operations and verify with differential fixtures.
close_reason: Implemented CIR is_volatile handling for loads and stores with std::ptr::read_volatile/write_volatile, added volatile.c fixture, added generated-Rust assertion for volatile intrinsics, extended BNF fuzz coverage and docs. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo run --quiet -- emit-fixtures, cargo test -- --nocapture, and git diff --check.

title: Remove unsound struct derives
description: Struct lowering should not derive Clone, Copy, or Default without proving every field supports those traits.
close_reason: Removed unsound Clone/Copy/Default derives from generated structs and kept explicit field initialization. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo run --quiet -- emit-fixtures, and cargo test -- --nocapture.

title: Recover tagged unions as Rust enums with data
description:
Why: the tag-plus-union idiom (a struct with an enum/int discriminant field plus a union field, where each union arm is only ever accessed under a matching discriminant check) is extremely common in C and has no idiomatic Rust equivalent today — it can only render as #[repr(C)] union + manual tag bookkeeping, never a safe enum. This is likely the single highest-value uncovered idiom.

What to do:
- New fact: a struct has a discriminant field and a union field where every union-arm access is provably guarded by a matching switch(tag)/if(tag==X) check on the discriminant.
- Rewrite: collapse the struct into a genuine Rust enum Variant { A(T1), B(T2), ... }, and rewrite tag-guarded union field accesses into match arms.
- Whole-program in scope (need to see every access site of the struct type to prove guard-safety), so likely needs new fact-collector scope similar to the Result recovery ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Fact collector proves discriminant-guarded union access for a candidate struct type across the whole program. Rewrite emits a real Rust enum and match-based accessors. Differential tests pass on fixtures with 2+ variants, nested access, and at least one case where the guard can't be proven (must stay on baseline union path).

title: Recover out-params as tuple/struct return values
description:
Why: C functions commonly pass a second (or third) return value through a pointer out-parameter (e.g. int parse(const char *s, int *out)). Baseline lowering keeps this as a raw pointer write, which is unidiomatic and forces callers to pre-declare and pass &mut locals.

What to do:
- New fact: a pointer parameter is write-only (never read before written, not aliased/escaped, written on every return path) — a disguised second return value.
- Rewrite: fold provably write-only out-params into the function's return type as a tuple (2 values) or generated named struct (3+), and rewrite call sites to destructure the result instead of pre-declaring an out local.
- Composes with the existing string_params/slice_index/ptr_len fact families and pointer-provenance neighborhood in the pass sequence.
acceptance_criteria: New fact collector proves out-param write-only-ness per function. New rewrite pass folds it into return type + rewrites call sites. Differential tests pass; fixture covers single and multi out-param cases.

title: Recover status-code returns as Result<T, E>
description:
Why: many C functions follow an errno-style convention: return 0/negative for success/failure, with callers only ever comparing the return value against 0 (never using it arithmetically). This is Rust's Result<T, E> idiom in disguise, but baseline lowering leaves it as a raw int with libc-style checks.

What to do:
- New fact: a function's return value is only ever compared against 0/negative at every call site (whole-program, not per-function — this needs new fact-collector scope beyond current per-function FixupFacts).
- Rewrite: convert the function to return Result<T, i32> (or a generated error enum), and propagate ? at call sites that immediately check-and-bail in the same status-code style.
- Higher risk than most fixups since it changes call-site control-flow shape everywhere the function is called, not just the callee body. Scope carefully; may need to start with a conservative subset (e.g. static functions with a closed set of call sites) before considering exported/API functions.
acceptance_criteria: Fact collector proves status-code convention across all call sites of a candidate function. Rewrite changes signature + call sites together, preserving control flow via ?. Differential tests pass on new fixtures; explicitly scoped to avoid rewriting functions whose return value is used non-boolean-ly anywhere.

title: Emit #[unsafe(no_mangle)] for externally-linked C symbols
description:
Why: emit_pub mode currently grants pub visibility to externally-linked items (src/lower.rs, the linkage_is_external(op) gate feeding the emit_pub Visibility::Pub branch) but attaches no symbol-name-preserving attribute. Rust's default mangling means the emitted pub fn/static does not actually keep the C symbol name, so any C caller expecting to link against e.g. void foo(void) cannot find it -- pub alone does not give C ABI linkage. This is the foundational gap all other jep.4 sub-tickets build on: weak, used/retain, and alias all attach to an already-externally-visible, correctly-named symbol.

What to do:
- In src/lower.rs, wherever linkage_is_external(op) currently gates Visibility::Pub, also attach a no-mangle marker to the emitted Item (function or static).
- Add an Item-level attribute variant in src/rust_ast.rs (e.g. Attr::NoMangle) rather than string-formatting; extend the existing Attr enum used for Allow/Repr/Derive.
- In src/codegen.rs, render it edition-2024-correctly: #[unsafe(no_mangle)] not bare #[no_mangle] (confirmed empirically: rustc --edition 2024 hard-errors E0658 'unsafe attribute used without unsafe' on bare #[no_mangle]).
- Only apply to items with CIR linkage == 0 (ExternalLinkage) that are actual definitions with a fixed C name.
- Internal linkage (CIR linkage == 7, InternalLinkage/static) must NOT get no_mangle -- keep current private-visibility behavior.
design: CIR linkage attr (attr_int(op, "linkage")) is the sole source of truth; no AST JSON needed. Confirmed encoding matches LLVM GlobalValue::LinkageTypes: External=0, Internal=7. Reuses the existing linkage_is_external() helper already in src/lower.rs -- this ticket extends its consumer, not the detection logic itself.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture: a C function and a C global with external linkage translated with emit_pub produce #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn/static in the generated Rust; nm/readelf on the compiled cdylib shows the undecorated C symbol name present. A static (internal-linkage) counterpart fixture confirms no no_mangle is emitted and the symbol does not appear in the dynamic symbol table. cargo fmt/cargo nextest r --release green.
notes: Empirically verified on local nightly (rustc 1.99.0-nightly): #[unsafe(no_mangle)] compiles cleanly under --edition 2024; bare #[no_mangle] is a hard E0658 error under that edition.
close_reason: Implemented typed no_mangle attributes and ABI-qualified external-linkage definitions. External emit_pub functions now render #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn, external globals render #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub static mut, and internal-linkage items remain private/unmangled. Verified with cargo test --test cross_tu and cargo nextest r --release on work/slate-jep.8 before merge.

title: Lower noreturn attributes into Rust never-returning signatures and call flow
description:
Why: noreturn affects function type, reachability, and dead code after calls. Preserving it can improve correctness around functions that exit, abort, or longjmp-style escape.

What to do:
- Add fixtures for __attribute__((noreturn)) and any _Noreturn spelling already visible to Clang.
- Extract noreturn facts from AST/CIR.
- Lower definitions/prototypes to Rust return type ! where the body/callee shape supports it, or keep conservative return type with explicit diagnostics otherwise.
- Ensure call sites after noreturn calls do not require fake fallthrough values.

Acceptance: noreturn fixtures compile and match C behavior; generated signatures use ! where supported; unsupported non-returning mechanisms are diagnosed explicitly.
close_reason: Merged: noreturn attributes lowered to Rust never-returning signatures in 622b28f (main 40490d8)

title: Lower __attribute__((constructor)) and __attribute__((destructor)) lifecycle hooks
description:
Why: constructor/destructor attributes change program lifecycle behavior and are common in C libraries for registration, counters, and process setup/teardown. Rust has no direct portable source-level equivalent, so Slate needs deliberate lowering or a clear unsupported diagnostic.

What to do:
- Add fixtures with constructor-only, destructor-only, and multiple priority-ordered hooks if Clang exposes priorities.
- Inspect Clang AST JSON and CIR/linkage output to identify where the attribute facts are available.
- Choose a Rust representation, likely platform/linker-section based init/fini arrays or generated runtime registration where supported.
- Preserve order where C requires it, and explicitly diagnose unsupported crate/target shapes.

Acceptance: fixtures prove hooks run before/after main when supported; generated Rust compiles and links on the default target; unsupported priority/target combinations produce intentional diagnostics rather than silently dropping hooks.
close_reason: Merged: constructor/destructor attributes lowered in 2103fb7

title: Lower packed and aligned record attributes into Rust repr attributes
description:
Why: packed/aligned attributes affect ABI layout, field offsets, and pointer safety. Dropping them can produce wrong generated Rust even if field access appears to compile.

What to do:
- Extract GNU/Clang packed and aligned attributes for structs/unions from AST facts.
- Lower to #[repr(C, packed)] / #[repr(C, packed(N))] / #[repr(C, align(N))] where Rust can express the layout.
- Audit field access for packed records so generated Rust avoids creating unaligned references.
- Add layout-sensitive fixtures using sizeof, alignof, offsetof, and field reads/writes.

Acceptance: packed/aligned fixture outputs match C; generated Rust uses the correct repr attributes; unaligned field access is handled safely or rejected.
notes: touches: src/lower.rs, tests/fixtures/
close_reason: Merged: packed/aligned record attributes lowered in eec7985

title: Lower C attributes with semantic Rust equivalents
description:
Why: Slate currently focuses on CIR operations and core type/layout facts, but C attributes can carry real semantics: lifecycle hooks, ABI/linkage, layout, allocation contracts, nullability, and control-flow facts. These are not optional fixups; when an attribute affects behavior, layout, or linkage, baseline lowering must preserve it or explicitly reject it.

What to do:
- Extract relevant GNU/Clang attributes from Clang AST JSON or CIR attrs where available.
- Lower behavior-affecting attributes into Rust items, ABI/linker attributes, runtime support, or explicit diagnostics.
- Keep optimization-only attributes as facts only when they can safely improve later analysis.
- Add one focused fixture per attribute family and verify with differential tests or compile/link shape tests as appropriate.

Out of scope: cosmetic-only source preservation unless it helps a semantic attribute.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level attribute families are tracked as children; implemented children add focused fixtures, preserve behavior/layout/linkage or diagnose unsupported semantics, and document the source of truth for attribute facts.

title: Emit __builtin_assume as core::hint::assert_unchecked under UB-preserving mode
description:
Why: cir.assume is currently dropped, which is correct as a conservative optimizer-hint erasure but loses the source-level UB assumption. Rust has core::hint::assert_unchecked for exactly this kind of unchecked assumption, but emitting it is unsafe and makes false assumptions immediate undefined behavior.

What to do:
- Add a fixture for __builtin_assume and inspect the emitted cir.assume shape.
- Decide whether this is a default lowering change, an opt-in translation mode, or a fixup gated by an explicit UB-preserving policy.
- If implemented, emit unsafe { core::hint::assert_unchecked(cond) } with the condition preserved exactly and no extra runtime check.
- Keep a conservative path that can still erase the hint when Slate is not preserving optimizer assumptions.

Assumption: this is only valid when Slate intentionally preserves C's UB contract for violated assumptions.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover true and guarded assumption shapes; generated Rust uses core::hint::assert_unchecked only in the chosen UB-preserving path; default behavior and docs make the UB tradeoff explicit; cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Implemented cir.assume lowering to unsafe core::hint::assert_unchecked, added true and guarded __builtin_assume fixture coverage, documented the UB-preserving contract, and verified with cargo fmt plus cargo nextest r --release.

title: Promote atomic globals to native AtomicN storage
description: Why: fixtures such as tests/fixtures/mt-atomics.c already translate correctly, but file-scope _Atomic objects still lower as static mut primitive storage accessed through unsafe AtomicN::from_ptr(addr_of_mut!(...)). That keeps unnecessary unsafe in threaded code and obscures the intended std::sync::atomic storage shape.\n\nWhat to do: add a conservative fact/fixup path for file-scope integer/bool atomic globals that are only accessed through matching atomic operations, rewrite their static initializer to AtomicN::new(...), rewrite matching atomic places to AtomicPlace::Local, and leave ambiguous globals on the baseline path. Add output-shape coverage for mt-atomics and keep differential tests green.
acceptance_criteria: mt-atomics generated Rust emits static counter: std::sync::atomic::AtomicI32 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicI32::new(0); atomic counter uses call counter.fetch_add/load directly without unsafe AtomicI32::from_ptr(addr_of_mut!(counter)); ambiguous or mismatched global uses remain on the baseline path; cargo fmt and focused differential tests pass.
notes: touches: src/fixups/facts/atomic_locals.rs, src/fixups/rewrite/atomic_locals.rs, src/fixups/mod.rs, tests/differential.rs
close_reason: Implemented conservative atomic global promotion in the atomic storage fixup. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Clean up non-volatile integer bit builtin temps
description: integer_bit_builtin_ops.c currently uses volatile inputs, forcing separate volatile reads. Make the fixture non-volatile and improve builtin temp generation so generated integer_bit_builtin_ops.rs does not keep pure result/copy temps around clz/ctz/popcount/parity/ffs/clrsb. Preserve volatile behavior for genuinely volatile fixtures.

title: Lower for-loop continue as direct structured control flow
description: Why: tests/fixtures.generated/continue_for.rs and tests/fixtures.generated/loop_break_continue.rs still lower C for-loop continue into synthetic labels and labeled blocks like '__continue0: { ... break '__continue0; }' plus labeled loop breaks. The original C fixtures are straightforward for loops with break/continue and should emit direct structured Rust, not workaround blocks or state-machine-like labels. Evidence: continue_while.rs and break_for.rs are already simple loop/break/continue forms, but continue_for.rs wraps the body so the step expression runs after a C continue. Root area: src/lower.rs lower_for/lower_for_loop_body/lower_continue, especially the LoopFrame continue_label path around lines 347-354 and 4771-4833. What to do: teach for-loop lowering or a narrow post-lowering fixup to represent the step explicitly so C continue lowers to a real continue target without '__continue blocks. Likely shape: split the loop body into condition, body, explicit step, and make continue jump to the step before looping, while preserving break and nested-loop behavior. Verify against continue_for.c and loop_break_continue.c.

title: Densify the compare_exchange result/expected chain
description:
Why: each atomic_compare_exchange_strong currently expands to a 4-temp chain: 'let _v34: Result<i32,i32> = ...compare_exchange(...); let _v35 = match _v34 { Ok(v)|Err(v) => v }; let _v36 = _v34.is_ok(); let _v37 = !_v36; if _v37 { expected = _v35; } cmpxchg_bool = _v36;'. The C pattern (write expected on failure, yield success bool) maps to one dense match.

What to do: add a fixup recognizing the lowered cmpxchg chain shape and rewriting it to 'ok = match a.compare_exchange(expected, desired, succ, fail) { Ok(_) => true, Err(v) => { expected = v; false } };' (or '.is_ok()' when the expected out-param is provably unused afterward). At minimum the '!is_ok' double negation must go. Keep baseline lowering (src/lower.rs lower_atomic_cmpxchg) as the correct verbose form; the strong-only policy (never compare_exchange_weak, to avoid spurious-failure divergence in differential runs) must be preserved.

Verify: differential atomics test passes; both success and failure cmpxchg paths in the fixture stay correct (ok=1/expected untouched, bad=0/expected2 updated to 42).
acceptance_criteria:
- cmpxchg lowers to a single match (or is_ok) expression per call after fixups.
- Failure path still writes back the observed value to the expected local.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Implemented a late atomic compare_exchange fixup that rewrites the result/value/is_ok/negation/failure-write chain into a single match expression preserving expected writeback. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Inline single-use atomic result temps into their bindings
description:
Why: even after lowerer-side alloca forwarding, atomic results that survive as temps ('atomic_temp = a.fetch_add(...); fa = atomic_temp;') should collapse to 'fa = a.fetch_add(...)' and then fuse with the zero-init declaration into 'let fa = a.fetch_add(5, Ordering::SeqCst);'. Existing pure-temp inlining refuses side-effecting expressions, so atomic calls need an order-preserving single-use inline: safe only when the temp's sole use is the immediately following statement with no intervening effects.

What to do: extend the effects facts (src/fixups/facts/effects.rs) and the inline-temps family (src/fixups/rewrite/inline_temps.rs or a sibling) to permit adjacent single-use inlining of Atomic* expressions. Cover match arms / dispatch bodies via the shared walkers so goto-fallback functions benefit too.

Verify: differential tests pass; atomics.rs shows 'let fa = ...fetch_add(...)' shape with no atomic_temp intermediary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Atomic fetch/swap/load results bind directly to their named local.
- Inlining only fires for adjacent single-use with no intervening effectful statement.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Implemented adjacent atomic result temp chaining and late zero-init declaration sinking so atomics.c emits direct let bindings for load/fetch/swap results. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Promote non-escaping _Atomic locals to native AtomicN storage
description:
Why: an atomic_int local currently keeps plain integer storage ('let mut a: i32 = 0') and every access re-derives 'unsafe { AtomicI32::from_ptr(std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(a)) }'. When the local's address never escapes non-atomically, this is pure noise: the local can own AtomicN storage and every access becomes a safe direct method call.

What to do:
- Add a fact (src/fixups/facts/) proving a local is only accessed through AtomicN::from_ptr(addr_of_mut!(local)) atomic ops (plus its initializer and plain reads expressible as atomic loads, e.g. the final '(int)a' cast in the fixture).
- Add a rewrite fixup (src/fixups/rewrite/) that changes the declaration to 'let a = AtomicI32::new(init);' and rewrites each access to a direct call on 'a', dropping the unsafe blocks and from_ptr wrappers.
- AST-to-AST only per docs/writing-a-fixup.md; use the shared walkers (facts/walk.rs, support/walk.rs). Baseline lowering stays as-is — disabling this fixup must still leave correct Rust.

Verify: differential atomics test passes; output-shape assertion that atomics.rs contains no from_ptr and no unsafe for the promoted local.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fact collector proves non-escape; conservative on any address escape or non-atomic write.
- Fixture local 'a' becomes AtomicI32 storage with safe method calls.
- Disabling the fixup still yields correct (verbose) Rust.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Atomic ops now carry AtomicPlace (Ptr unsafe from_ptr view vs Local safe direct call); baseline unsafe moved from codegen into an explicit Expr::Unsafe in the lowerer. New fact facts/atomic_locals.rs proves a local int slot is only named as the pointer operand of matching-width atomic ops; rewrite/atomic_locals.rs re-declares it as AtomicN::new(init) and unwraps ops to safe direct calls. atomics.rs now has zero unsafe/from_ptr; escaping/global atomics stay on baseline. Verified with cargo nextest r --release (513 passed incl. 4 new unit tests + new shape test).

title: Forward per-call CIR atomic temp allocas in the lowerer
description:
Why: clang emits a fresh .atomictmp alloca for each atomic op's value operand and an atomic-temp alloca for each result. Slate's lowerer hoists every one as a named local, so tests/fixtures.generated/atomics.rs opens with ~15 shadowed 'let mut _atomictmp'/'let mut atomic_temp' declarations, and zero_init fuses the first store's value into the last shadow's initializer — correct only by accident of shadowing order, and unreadable.

What to do: in src/lower.rs, recognize these single-store-then-single-load compiler temps and forward the stored value directly instead of materializing a named local: 'a.store(100, SeqCst)' rather than '_atomictmp = 100; ...store(_atomictmp, ...)', and bind results straight to their consumer slot instead of routing through atomic_temp. This is baseline-lowering work (correctness must not depend on any fixup); keep the named-local path for allocas that genuinely have multiple stores or escape.

Verify: differential test for atomics.c passes; generated output has zero shadowed _atomictmp/atomic_temp declarations; full nextest suite green.
acceptance_criteria:
- No shadowed compiler-temp declarations in atomics.rs.
- Atomic operand values appear inline in the atomic call expression.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Lowerer now forwards single-store/single-load compiler-temp allocas (.atomictmp, atomic-temp, cmpxchg.bool) as SSA values instead of hoisting shadowed named locals; non-literal values snapshot into immutable temps at the store site. Verified with cargo nextest r --release (508 passed) and a new output-shape test asserting no _atomictmp/atomic_temp/cmpxchg_bool locals and inline atomic operands.

title: Lower atomics densely to idiomatic std::sync::atomic
acceptance_criteria:
- atomics.rs contains no shadowed _atomictmp/atomic_temp declarations; atomic operands inline into the call site.
- A non-escaping local atomic_int lowers (via facts+fixup) to AtomicI32 storage with safe direct method calls; no unsafe/from_ptr for it.
- The compare_exchange chain collapses to a single dense expression per call.
- memory_order/atomic_flag items are not emitted when unused.
- Differential tests pass throughout; correctness never depends on a fixup.
- Fuzzer (tests/support/cgen.rs) and c.bnf cover the atomic subset.

Use tests/fixtures/array_init.c as the regression.

Reproduce today's three structured shapes from the dispatch loop: linear chain -> straight-line (goto_forward); single-block back-edge -> loop{...; if !cond break} (goto_backward_loop); one non-entry cycle -> peel entry/exit, residual loop{match __blockN} (goto_irreducible).
