title: Lower static goto CFG regions with localized state loops
description:
Why: c2rust avoids whole-function dispatch for many goto cases by emitting acyclic prefixes/tails as straight-line code and confining state-machine matching to cyclic CFG regions. Slate should try the same conservative representation for static goto CFGs.

What to do:
- Replace the narrow forward-goto experiment with a localized CFG-region lowering path before full dispatch fallback.
- Emit simple acyclic forward goto regions as straight-line code, skipping unreachable blocks.
- Emit closed cyclic static regions with a local loop/match state and break to a shared successor tail when exits agree.
- Preserve full dispatch fallback for dynamic/computed indirect targets and shapes the localized path cannot prove.
- Add output-shape assertions for forward goto, backward loop, irreducible static cycle, and fallback fixtures.

Acceptance criteria:
- goto_forward.c emits no __state0 or __dispatch0 and omits unreachable x = 99.
- goto_irreducible.c emits straight-line prelude/tail with a localized loop/match for the cycle rather than whole-function dispatch.
- dynamic/computed and unsupported nested goto fixtures still use dispatch fallback.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Added SCC-based localized static goto lowering: acyclic direct-forward chains linearize, single static cyclic SCCs lower to local loop/match state with shared tail, and dynamic/unsupported shapes keep full dispatch fallback. Verified with cargo fmt, focused differential shape tests, generated_differential, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Lower simple reducible backward goto loops as structured Rust loops
description:
Why: goto_backward_loop.c should not need the dispatch fallback. Its CFG is a preheader plus a single natural loop with one exit, which can lower directly to Rust loop/break form and then feed existing cleanup passes.

What to do:
- Add a try_lower_structured_goto path before lower_dispatch emits __state/__dispatch.
- For the proven simple natural-loop shape, emit preheader statements, loop body statements, inverted-exit break, and tail statements.
- Preserve the existing dispatch fallback for unsupported shapes.
acceptance_criteria: - tests/fixtures/goto_backward_loop.c emits a structured loop without __state0 or __dispatch0.\n- The generated Rust remains differentially equivalent.\n- Unsupported goto fixtures still use the dispatch fallback and pass existing tests.
close_reason: Added a conservative structured goto path for preheader plus single self-loop backward goto regions, preserving dispatch fallback for unsupported shapes. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Run temp inlining and simple cleanup inside match arms
description:
Why: fallback dispatch output is much noisier than necessary because some cleanup passes do not enter Stmt::Match arms. tests/fixtures/goto_backward_loop.c shows temp chains inside match arms that should be eligible for normal cleanup even if dispatch remains the fallback.

What to do:
- Update inline_temps traversal to use shared nested-body helpers or explicitly handle Stmt::Match arms.
- Audit nearby simple cleanup passes for bespoke recursion that skips match arms.
- Keep behavior-preserving guards unchanged; this is traversal coverage, not new semantic reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: - Single-use pure temps inside match arms are inlined when the same pattern would be inlined in a plain body.\n- Existing dispatch state-machine tests remain correct.\n- Add an output-shape or unit test proving cleanup reaches a match arm.
close_reason: Implemented match-arm traversal for inline_temps and compound_assign using shared nested-body walkers. Added unit tests for match-arm cleanup and a goto_backward_loop output-shape assertion. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo test.

title: Add CFG analysis helper for reducible goto lowering
description:
Why: structured goto recovery should be driven by CIR block graph shape, not by ad hoc source-looking goto patterns after the state machine has been emitted.

What to do:
- Build a small CFG view over CIR Region blocks used by lower_dispatch.
- Classify successors, labels, entry block, backedges, and exits.
- Compute enough dominance or reducibility information to identify single-entry natural loops and reject irreducible or dynamic indirect-branch cases.
- Keep this helper independent from Rust fixup passes.
acceptance_criteria: - The helper can identify the CFG shape for goto_backward_loop.c as a single-entry natural loop.\n- The helper rejects indirect/dynamic state targets and irreducible multi-entry regions.\n- Unit tests cover forward-only goto, simple backward loop, and an irreducible or unsupported graph.
close_reason: Added dispatch CFG analysis helper with dominance, natural-loop, dynamic target, and irreducible-cycle coverage; cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo nextest r --release pass.

title: Improve goto code generation and cleanup
description:
Why: goto-bearing functions currently lower directly to a conservative __state/__dispatch match loop. That is correct as a fallback, but it prevents existing Rust cleanup passes from seeing easier loop/if shapes and produces very temp-heavy fallback output.

What to do:
- Keep the state-machine dispatch as the correctness fallback for arbitrary or irreducible control flow.
- Add structured CFG lowering for reducible goto patterns before dispatch is emitted.
- Make cleanup passes enter Stmt::Match arms so fallback dispatch output is still improved.
- Cover tests/fixtures/goto_backward_loop.c and additional forward/irreducible/scope-sensitive goto cases.
acceptance_criteria:
- goto_backward_loop.c no longer emits the dispatch state machine when the CFG is proven structurally reducible.
- Fallback dispatch arms still get normal temp/compound/printf cleanup where safe.
- Unsupported or irreducible goto CFGs still lower correctly through the existing state-machine fallback.
- Differential tests and output-shape assertions cover structured and fallback paths.

title: Recover printf calls in array initialization fixtures
description:
Why: array_init.c currently leaves all printf calls raw even though the formats are simple: %d, %d %d, %s, and %s %d. The generated Rust has c-string format pointers and arguments that are already mostly safe Rust expressions, including array indexes, a lifted &str passed as s.as_ptr(), and a padded local i8 array passed via as_mut_ptr().

What to do: investigate why printf_format/stdio recovery rejects these callsites. Extend fact-backed printf recovery to handle the array_init shapes where the format string is a C string literal cast to *mut i8 and arguments are scalar locals/indexes, lifted &str pointers for %s, or proven nul-terminated local char arrays for %s. Leave raw printf in place when a %s argument is not proven nul-terminated or otherwise safe to format as Rust string data.

Use tests/fixtures/array_init.c as the regression.
design: Keep this in the fixup layer and reuse existing printf/string facts where possible. The proof should be argument-shape based, not tied to variable names in array_init.
acceptance_criteria: array_init generated Rust recovers the simple printf calls to print!/println! where arguments are proven safe, including integer array indexes and string arguments for the lifted string/local padded char array cases. The output no longer contains a retained printf extern solely for array_init. Unsupported or unproved %s arguments remain raw. Differential tests remain green.
notes: touches: src/fixups/facts/printf.rs, src/fixups/rewrite/printf_format.rs, tests/fixtures/array_init.c, tests/differential.rs
close_reason: Implemented printf recovery for array_init C-string formats and proven local/lifted string arguments. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Recover array index counted loops as for-range loops
description:
Why: array_init.c contains a canonical counted array loop, for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { sum += a[i]; }, but generated Rust still emits a scoped mutable i plus loop/break form. This is correct but noisy, and it blocks idiomatic array iteration/index loop recovery.

What to do: investigate why the existing counted/range loop facts do not recognize this shape after current fixups. Add or extend fact-backed loop recovery so a simple initializer, strict upper bound, unit increment, and body using a[i] can become a Rust for-range loop. The first target shape can be for i in 0..5 { sum += a[i as usize]; } or a more idiomatic proven array iteration form if existing facts support it safely.

Use tests/fixtures/array_init.c as the regression.
design: Keep this as a fixup fact/rewrite improvement. Do not bind the rewrite to array names; prove the counted loop shape from initializer, condition, increment, and induction variable uses.
acceptance_criteria: array_init generated Rust no longer contains the raw let mut i + loop + if !(i < 5) break shape for the sum loop. Output-shape coverage proves a for loop is emitted, and differential tests remain green. Unsupported loops with ambiguous bounds, non-unit increments, escapes, or mutation of the induction variable outside the increment remain on the baseline loop path.
notes: Investigation: the existing counted-loop/range-loop path is working for varargs.c. It records loops whose bound is a binding, then range_loop renders 0..bound, which is why for (i = 0; i < n; i++) becomes for _ in 0..n. array_init.c fails because the loop bound is the literal 5. counted_loop::unique_binding_for_bound currently rejects non-Var bounds, and range_loop expects fact.bound to name a binding. slice_loop/loop_shapes also focus on slices or len aliases, not local fixed arrays with literal bounds. The implementation should extend the existing counted-loop facts/rewrite to represent literal or const-expression bounds, and optionally prove literal equals local array length for a later iter/enumerate form.
close_reason: Implemented counted loop recovery for literal, variable, and arithmetic expression bounds; array_init now emits a for range loop and full release nextest passes.

title: Recover buffer pointer cursors as indexed array writes
description:
Why: C code often stores start/current/end pointers into a small buffer struct and mutates through the current pointer. In anon_local_struct.c, buf.start and buf.pointer both point at storage, buf.end is storage + 4, writes through *buf.pointer fill storage[0] and storage[1], and pointer subtraction reports cursor and capacity. The current Rust keeps this shape as raw pointers even though the backing array and cursor increments are locally proven.

What to do: add fact-backed fixups that recognize buffer-like structs whose pointer fields are initialized from the same local array, track a current pointer as an index cursor, and rewrite proven deref writes/increments/subtractions to indexed array operations. Treat one-past-end pointers such as storage + 4 as exclusive bounds, not as safe references; the lifted representation should use an index/length fact for end so OOB provenance does not block safe Rust recovery.

Suggested shape: facts should connect buf.start, buf.pointer, and buf.end to the same backing array with roles start/current/end_exclusive. The rewrite can turn *buf.pointer = expr into storage[idx] = expr, buf.pointer++ into idx += 1, buf.pointer - buf.start into idx, and buf.end - buf.start into storage.len() or the proven bound. Keep this in fixups; baseline raw-pointer lowering remains the fallback.
design: Represent C one-past-end pointer facts as exclusive integer bounds over the backing array rather than Rust references. Lift only dereferenceable current-pointer positions; end_exclusive is usable for subtraction/capacity comparisons but never for indexing or address-of recovery.
acceptance_criteria: anon_local_struct.c has output-shape coverage showing storage writes via safe indexes, cursor/capacity differences without offset_from, and no unsafe raw pointer derefs for the proven buffer cursor case. The implementation refuses to lift when start/current/end do not share the same backing array or when the current pointer may escape/alias unpredictably.
close_reason: Implemented fact-backed buffer pointer field provenance and a guarded buffer cursor rewrite that converts proven local pointer deref writes and same-array pointer distances to safe array indexes while treating one-past-end fields as exclusive bounds. Added unit coverage for arbitrary field names, one-past deref rejection, escaping alias rejection, and anon_local_struct output-shape coverage. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo fmt, and cargo nextest run --release.

title: Recover anonymous local structs as generated tuple structs
description:
Why: local anonymous C structs currently render as verbose named-field struct boilerplate even when the source only needs a local anonymous aggregate such as struct { int x; int y; } point = {3, 4};. Plain Rust tuples are too weak for later field/pointer rewrite passes because field identity and an addressable nominal type disappear.

What to do: add fact gathering for local anonymous struct types and a conservative AST-to-AST fixup that emits a generated tuple struct type such as __slate_anonymous_struct_0, rewrites eligible local declarations/initializers to positional construction, and rewrites field accesses to tuple-field accesses where facts prove the mapping. Add a real Rust AST node for tuple struct items rather than rendering raw text. Keep unsupported mutable/pointer-heavy cases on the baseline path until field/pointer rewrites can prove them safe.

Use anon_local_struct.c as the main regression.
acceptance_criteria: anon_local_struct generated Rust contains a generated tuple struct item for the anonymous local struct and initializes point positionally, without the previous named-field local struct boilerplate for the eligible case. Field reads still compile and differential tests pass. The implementation includes focused fact/fixup coverage and does not use rendered string rewriting.
close_reason: Recovered anonymous local structs as generated tuple structs with fact-backed field mapping and a TupleStructLit AST node. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo fmt, and cargo nextest run --release.

title: Thread constant main retval through final exit cleanup
description:
Why: late rewrites can leave main with __retval initialized/stored as 0, copied through a temp, and passed to std::process::exit even though the exit status is statically zero. This keeps boilerplate in fixtures after other cleanup passes succeed.

What to do: improve the fixup pipeline so a final constant __retval store feeding the main exit temp collapses to std::process::exit(0), allowing the existing zero-exit cleanup to remove it. Keep the rewrite AST-based and conservative; do not rely on rendered text.

Use address_of_array_element as the main regression.
acceptance_criteria: The address_of_array_element generated Rust no longer contains __retval or std::process::exit for the final zero status. The cleanup still preserves nonzero/dynamic main exit statuses and differential tests pass.
close_reason: Threaded final main __retval stores through the exit temp, removing earlier pure retval writes when the slot is otherwise unread. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo fmt, and cargo nextest run --release.

title: Add facts for array-element pointer origins
description: Why: rewrites for &array[index] pointers need a semantic proof that a pointer binding denotes a specific element of a specific array binding. Matching rendered addr_of_mut output in rewrite code would be brittle and would miss equivalent forms.\n\nWhat to do: add a fact collector for local pointer origins. Record pointer binding, base array binding, index expression, mutability, and source path for direct forms such as let p = std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(values[1]) and p = std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(values[1]). Keep v1 conservative: local arrays only, constant indexes, no volatile/atomic places, and only bindings whose provenance assignment is unambiguous. Consider recognizing values.as_mut_ptr().add(k) only if the AST shape is already available and equally proven.
acceptance_criteria: FixupFacts exposes array-element pointer origin facts with stable binding IDs and paths. Unit coverage proves origins are collected for direct let/assign addr_of array-index forms and rejected for non-array bases, non-constant/unsupported indexes, ambiguous pointer writes, and volatile/atomic contexts.
close_reason: Added array-element pointer origin facts with unit coverage. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo fmt, and cargo nextest run --release.

title: Rewrite proven array-element pointers to safe indexes
description: Why: once pointer bindings are proven to denote specific array elements, local derefs and same-base pointer differences can be rendered as safe Rust indexes and integer index differences instead of unsafe raw-pointer operations.\n\nWhat to do: add a rewrite pass consuming array-element pointer origin facts. Rewrite unsafe {*p} to values[index] when p has a proven origin, rewrite q.offset_from(p) to index_q - index_p when both origins share the same base array, and prune now-dead pointer/temp bindings through existing cleanup where possible. Use the address_of_array_elements fixture as the main regression.
acceptance_criteria: The address_of_array_elements generated Rust prints via values[1] + values[3] and the same-base pointer difference 3 - 1 or an equivalent constant/index expression. The output no longer contains unsafe pointer derefs or offset_from for this fixture. Differential tests still pass.
close_reason: Rewrote proven array-element pointer derefs and same-base pointer differences to safe indexes. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo fmt, and cargo nextest run --release.

title: (EPIC) Recover array-element pointer provenance
description: Why: address-of array elements currently lower to raw pointer temps, unsafe derefs, and offset_from calls even when both pointers have known provenance into the same local array. This keeps simple C like int *p = &values[1]; int *q = &values[3]; noisy and unnecessarily unsafe.\n\nWhat to do: add fact-backed fixups that model pointer bindings as pointing at a known array element, then rewrite local derefs and same-base pointer differences to safe indexed expressions where the proof is explicit. Keep this in the fixup layer; baseline lowering remains correct raw-pointer Rust.
acceptance_criteria: A sub-epic tracks pointer-origin fact collection and safe rewrites for array element addresses. The address_of_array_elements fixture is covered by output-shape assertions showing safe indexed accesses and a constant same-base pointer difference where applicable.

title: Fold immediate placeholder assignments after temp cleanup
description: Fold placeholder declarations followed by immediate assignment after late temp cleanup, including mutable declarations assigned immutable RHS values. Use the varargs fixture as regression: total should initialize directly to 0, first/second should initialize from ap.next_arg, and remove_mut should clean now-unwritten locals.
close_reason: Folded late placeholder assignments after temp cleanup and verified varargs output

title: Inline temp chains feeding immediate call arguments
description: Reduce synthetic _v bindings when they only feed the next call, method call, or printf/println-style expression in the same statement list. Use the varargs fixture as the regression target: inline literal/call argument temps in main and inline va_arg temps into source local assignments or compound assignments where safe. Keep this in the fact/rewrite temp-chain pipeline and preserve evaluation order.
close_reason: Split temp inlining into early and late passes with late temp reduction for call and assignment chains

title: Recover maybe_apply return branches from temp and retval chains
description:
Add the integration fixture for C code like static int maybe_apply(int (*op)(int), int value) { if (op) { return op(value); } return value; } and use the temp-chain plus retval facts/rewrite passes to recover direct return expressions inside the branch and fallthrough return. Ignore redundant scope removal; that remains slate-04q.22.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fixture output contains if op.is_some() { return op.unwrap()(value); } or equivalent direct return expression.
- Fixture output contains return value; for the fallthrough path.
- The maybe_apply function no longer contains __retval = _v...; return __retval; in either path.
- Differential behavior remains green and cargo nextest r --release passes.
notes: touches: src/fixups/rewrite/inline_temps.rs, src/fixups/rewrite/call_args.rs, tests/differential.rs
close_reason: Completed follow-up temp recovery for maybe_apply: Option presence checks now inline receiver temps to op.is_some(), Option unwrap receiver temps inline to op.unwrap(), and function-pointer call args inline to value. Verified with cargo fmt, focused inline_temps/call_args unit tests, function_pointer_presence differential shape test, generated_differential, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Add facts for collapsible single-use temp chains
description:
Collect fact records for temp bindings whose initializer can be substituted into their single read without changing evaluation order. Facts should include producer path, consumer path, source binding, dependency temps, and rejection/barrier reasons where useful. Start with same statement-list cases and existing def-use/effect/place/call facts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests record a collapsible chain for pure temps such as _v1 = op and _v2 = value.
- Unit tests reject chains crossing unknown calls, memory writes, or writes to values read by the initializer.
- Uses existing fact walk helpers and does not add pass-local recursive walkers.
- cargo fmt and focused tests pass.
notes: touches: src/fixups/facts/mod.rs, new temp-chain facts module, fact tests around def-use/effects/places/calls
close_reason: Implemented TempChainFact collection for conservative same-body movable-pure single-use temps, including dependency temp tracking and barrier rejection tests. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Rewrite pure single-use temp chains at use sites
description:
Use the temp-chain facts to replace pure single-use temp reads with their initializer expressions and remove the temporary lets. This should generalize current narrow inline temp behavior without inlining through type/coercion barriers.

Acceptance criteria:
- A fixture or unit test collapses _v1 = op; _v2 = value; consumer(_v1, _v2) into consumer(op, value).
- Rewrites are driven by temp-chain facts rather than rediscovering proof locally.
- Existing call argument pinning/type-safety guards remain respected.
- cargo fmt and focused tests pass.
notes: touches: src/fixups/facts/temp_chains.rs, src/fixups/rewrite/inline_temps.rs, src/fixups/support/walk.rs, tests/differential.rs
close_reason: Implemented temp-chain fact-driven inline temp rewrites, including nested expression and unsafe-wrapper consumers, and preserved call argument type-safety guards. Verified with cargo fmt, focused cargo test filters, generated_differential, and cargo nextest r --release before merge; post-merge cargo test was interrupted at user request after earlier suites passed.

title: Collapse effectful immediate temp into return-slot assignment
description:
Extend the temp-chain rewrite to handle an effectful value-producing temp only when it is consumed immediately by a return-slot assignment or return in the same statement list, so function-pointer calls like _v3 = op.unwrap()(value); __retval = _v3 can become __retval = op.unwrap()(value) without moving the call across unrelated code.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests collapse an immediate effectful call-result temp into a following __retval assignment.
- Unit tests reject the same collapse with intervening side effects or non-adjacent consumers.
- The proof is fact-backed and conservative about evaluation order.
- cargo fmt and focused tests pass.
notes: touches: src/fixups/facts/temp_chains.rs, src/fixups/rewrite/inline_temps.rs, tests/differential.rs
close_reason: Implemented fact-backed collapse for immediate effectful temp producers into return-slot assignments and direct returns. Added conservative fact and rewrite tests plus function_pointer_presence e2e shape coverage. Verified with cargo fmt, focused cargo test filters, generated_differential, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: (EPIC) Recover single-use temp chains in return paths
description:
Why: return-path lowering still preserves SSA-style temp chains such as maybe_apply: temps for op/value/function-pointer result, assignment into __retval, then return __retval. Existing retval collapse only handles adjacent return-slot round trips and does not recover the expression chain feeding them.

Goal: add fact-backed, incremental fixups that can safely collapse single-use temporary chains feeding return-slot assignments and returns, including inside branch bodies, without moving side effects across barriers.

Design direction:
- Collect facts that describe collapsible temp chains separately from rewriting.
- Start with conservative same-body/same-branch adjacency and barrier checks.
- Let retval collapse consume recovered assignments rather than embedding temp-chain logic in the retval pass.
- Keep higher-level idiom recovery, such as if-let for Option function pointers or redundant scope removal, as separate work.

title: Preserve source local names through lowering and fixups
description:
Generated Rust is still hard to read because many source locals and simple intermediate expressions survive as synthetic _v... temporaries instead of using the original C variable names or direct expressions. Add fixup/lowering support that carries source-level naming information far enough through the Rust AST pipeline to prefer original local names where semantics allow.

Scope:
- Identify where CIR/source AST location or declaration information can be mapped onto lowered Rust bindings.
- Preserve original variable names for locals/parameters instead of replacing readable source names with _v... temporaries when the binding is source-backed.
- Collapse or rename source-derived SSA temporaries only when doing so does not change evaluation order, aliasing, or borrow behavior.
- Keep baseline lowering correct if the cleanup is disabled; this belongs in the fixup/readability pipeline where possible.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add at least one regression fixture where generated Rust currently emits unreadable _v... bindings for source locals, and assert the improved output shape.
- The implementation uses existing rust_ast/fixup traversal helpers and fact collection patterns rather than private recursive walkers.
- Differential tests still cover the transformed program behavior.
- cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Verified source names are already preserved through lowering: function params come from CIR entry block arg names, source locals come from cir.alloca name attributes via sanitize_ident, and existing differential checks cover readable params/locals including add.c, pointers.c, and varargs.c. Remaining _v bindings are CIR temporaries/expression values covered by separate temp-chain cleanup work.

title: libyaml polish: mark public raw-pointer-dereferencing functions unsafe
description:
Generated libyaml public functions can dereference raw pointer parameters while remaining safe Rust functions, triggering lints such as: `this public function might dereference a raw pointer but is not marked unsafe` at generated `src/writer.rs:440` for `(*emitter).raw_buffer.pointer = _v239;`.

Fix Slate to mark generated public functions unsafe when their body may dereference raw pointers or otherwise requires an unsafe caller contract. This should preserve internal call sites by adding unsafe blocks/calls where needed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a fixture/regression for a public generated function that dereferences a raw pointer parameter.
- Regenerated libyaml marks the affected public functions unsafe or otherwise eliminates the lint without hiding it with an allow.
- Generated call sites still compile.
- `cargo nextest r --release` passes.
close_reason: Implemented unsafe function modifiers for public pointer-dereferencing generated APIs, propagated unsafe call-site wrapping across translation units, and kept generated Rust main safe. Added unsafe_public cross-TU regression. Verified with cargo nextest r --release.

title: libyaml polish: emit Rust c-string literals for nul-terminated C strings
description:
Generated libyaml emits manually nul-terminated byte strings like `b"write error\0".as_ptr() as *mut i8`, which triggers Rust warnings about manually constructing a nul-terminated string. Example from generated `src/writer.rs` around the `yaml_emitter_set_writer_error` call.

Fix Slate to emit C string literals using the Rust `c"..."` literal form where possible, with correct pointer casts for C APIs expecting `*mut i8`/`*const i8`. Leave byte-string fallback for non-UTF-8 or otherwise unsupported literals.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a fixture/regression for a C string literal passed to a C-style pointer API.
- Regenerated libyaml uses `c"write error"` or equivalent supported C string literal output for this case and no longer emits the manual-nul warning there.
- `cargo nextest r --release` passes.
close_reason: Implemented c-string literal fixup and verified libyaml writer output

title: libyaml polish: avoid function pointer comparisons against None
description:
Generated libyaml currently emits function pointer comparisons like `if _v3 != None`, which triggers Rust warnings that function pointer address comparisons are not meaningful. Example from generated `src/writer.rs`: `if _v3 != None`.

Fix Slate to emit the idiomatic/semantically correct presence check for optional function pointers, likely `.is_some()` / `.is_none()` on `Option<extern fn>` values rather than comparing against `None`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a small C fixture or focused regression that generates an optional function pointer check.
- Regenerated libyaml no longer warns on `if _v3 != None`-style function pointer comparisons.
- `cargo nextest r --release` passes.
close_reason: Implemented typed function-pointer null lowering to None and Option::is_some/is_none presence checks in src/lower.rs. Added tests/fixtures/function_pointer_presence.c regression. Verified with cargo nextest r --release.

title: libyaml tests: import generated crate APIs instead of unresolved externs
description:
Generated integration tests for a multi-file library crate can still emit body-less C declarations as unsafe extern "C" declarations even when the symbols are defined by the generated Rust library crate. In libyaml-crate this makes harness=false test binaries link against missing native symbols such as yaml_parser_initialize, yaml_parser_scan, yaml_token_delete, yaml_parser_delete, and yaml_parser_set_input_file instead of importing libyaml_crate::api or libyaml_crate::scanner functions.

Reproduction should use Slate's multi-crate compilation path, not manual edits to generated libyaml output. Add a fixture or regression test that runs translate-project --lib for a small multi-translation-unit C project where a test/support executable calls functions defined in another generated module. The generated test target should compile/link by importing the generated Rust crate APIs, and should fail before the fix with undefined symbols from extern "C" declarations.

Acceptance criteria:
- The generated library crate's integration-test sources resolve generated functions/globals through the generated crate root, e.g. libyaml_crate::<module>::<symbol>, instead of emitting extern "C" declarations for symbols defined in the generated project.
- The reproduction is automated through the multi-crate/library generation path so cargo check/test of the generated fixture verifies the behavior.
- Regenerating /home/takashi/libyaml into libyaml-crate or target/libyaml-crate produces runnable test targets without linker errors for generated libyaml APIs.
- cargo nextest r --release passes after the change.
close_reason: Implemented generated library-test symbol resolution via cross-module crate-root imports and harness=false test targets. Verified with cargo nextest r --release and libyaml regenerate/check/test-link commands.

title: libyaml tests: preserve string pointer locals used after init
description: Converted libyaml integration tests fail to compile because tests/test_reader.rs references bom_original without a declaration. The C source declares char *bom_original = "..."; and Slate likely drops the local during lowering/fixups while later uses remain. Reproduce with the libyaml generated crate tests, add a focused fixture, and fix the lowering/fixup path so string pointer locals used after initialization are preserved.
close_reason: Emitted C pointer globals initialized by #cir.global_view string literals, preserving bom_original in generated libyaml tests. Verified with cargo nextest r --release and fresh libyaml cargo check --lib --tests.

title: libyaml polish: emit shared C enums as Rust enums and reuse them from tests
description: Generated libyaml currently lowers C enums such as yaml_encoding_t to integer constants and repeats enum-like definitions across generated test modules. Recover C enum declarations as shared Rust enum types in the generated library crate, export them from the shared types module, and have out-of-module generated tests use the public enum/type rather than private duplicated integer constants. Keep ABI/layout correctness for C enum values and verify against ~/libyaml generation.
close_reason: Implemented shared Rust enum emission for recovered C enums, including library crate types.rs exports and generated integration-test imports. Verified with cargo nextest r --release and fresh libyaml generation plus cargo check --lib.

title: Add string lift/copy lift-plan facts
description: string_lift and string_copy still compute candidate liftability and pointer-view/printf allowability inside rewrite modules. Add facts that summarize lift plans and allowed string pointer uses so those rewrites can select already-proven candidates instead of running semantic allowability scans.
acceptance_criteria:
Facts under src/fixups/facts describe which string buffers are liftable for borrowed/owned recovery and which downstream pointer-view uses are allowed.
string_lift and string_copy consume those facts for liftability decisions instead of parsing printf formats or scanning downstream statements for semantic allowability.
Rewrites retain only AST mutation and local shape replacement.
Relevant string_lift, string_copy, fixups, and generated differential tests pass.
close_reason: Added StringLiftPlanFact and StringCopyRewriteFact collection under src/fixups/facts, fixed printf arg fact paths, and migrated string_lift/string_copy to consume those facts for liftability and copy rewrites. Verified with cargo test -q string_lift, cargo test -q string_copy, cargo test -q fixups, cargo test -q generated_differential, and cargo fmt && cargo test.

title: Split remaining rewrite-local semantic analysis into facts
description: Several rewrite passes still contain semantic/fact-like analysis even though the walker boundary now prevents shared immutable traversal from rewrite modules. Move the remaining semantic discovery into src/fixups/facts and keep rewrites as AST + FixupFacts -> AST'. Target modules include string_copy, string_lift, string_libc, call_args, and extern-pruning discovery in string rewrites.
acceptance_criteria:
string_copy, string_lift, and string_libc no longer compute semantic allowability, local string environments, printf/libc compatibility, or remaining extern-call discovery from ad hoc rewrite scans.
call_args removes or relocates obsolete local signature collection and consumes call facts for signature/callee information.
Any newly required facts are collected under src/fixups/facts and registered through facts::analyze.
Rewrite modules retain only local AST shape matching and mutation using FixupFacts.
Relevant fixup and generated differential tests pass.

Filed slate-oux.7 for the remaining string_lift/string_copy lift-plan facts. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test -q fixups, cargo test -q generated_differential, and cargo test.

Verified with cargo fmt and full cargo test.

Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test -q printf, and cargo test -q fixups. cargo test -q generated_differential now fails only known slate-oux.3 string_libc_fixup.

description: Move inline_temps, call_args, compound_assign, and drop_call_results decisions onto def-use, effect, callsite, value, and cast facts instead of local read-count and purity walkers in rewrite modules.
acceptance_criteria: The temp-related rewrite passes consume FixupFacts/fact APIs for use counts, purity, call pinning, and type/inference guards; duplicate semantic walkers are removed or reduced to mechanical AST rewrites; existing behavior tests pass.

Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo nextest r --release --no-fail-fast.

description: Audit and migrate rewrite passes so decisions are driven by facts produced under src/fixups/facts instead of each rewrite pass doing its own semantic analysis. This keeps fact gathering and AST rewriting separated and makes later cleanup passes reusable and easier to reason about.
acceptance_criteria: Each rewrite pass either consumes FixupFacts/fact APIs for semantic decisions or has a documented task explaining why it cannot yet; duplicate semantic walkers in rewrite passes are removed or ticketed; tests continue to cover behavior after migration.

Verified with cargo fmt && cargo nextest r --release from worktree and main.

title: Improve fixup fact gathering for richer Rust recovery
description: Add reusable fact-gathering passes that expose semantic information for future Rust idiomatization. These facts should let fixups share proof machinery instead of reimplementing local scans, and should unlock cleaner generated Rust while keeping baseline lowering correctness unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
New fact families are represented in FixupFacts or documented adjacent fact stores.
Each child pass has focused tests proving positive and rejected facts.
Consumers can use facts without depending on rendered Rust text.
Generated Rust remains behaviorally unchanged until consuming rewrite tickets intentionally change output.

title: Add stable semantic IDs and FixupFacts context
description: Introduce the minimal infrastructure needed to attach facts to semantic entities in the Rust AST/fixup pipeline: function IDs, binding IDs for params/locals, loop IDs, and a FixupFacts context passed to fact-backed rewrites. Traversal/expression IDs may exist for one phase only, but persistent facts should attach to semantic IDs or explicit relationship facts. This is the substrate for separating analysis from rewriting.
acceptance_criteria:
- Functions, params/locals, and loops can be identified consistently within a fact-analysis phase.
- FixupFacts can store facts keyed by semantic IDs and multi-entity relationship facts.
- The pipeline can run analysis before selected rewrites without changing baseline output.
- Tests cover ID assignment stability for ordinary functions, nested scopes, and loops.
notes: touches: src/fixups/facts/, src/fixups/mod.rs, src/rust_ast.rs or tests in fixups
close_reason: Implemented src/fixups/facts analysis scaffold with semantic FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId assignment, FixupFacts/AnalyzedProgram, no-op pipeline integration, and unit coverage for ordinary functions, nested scopes, branches, match arms, and loops. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Split fixup fact discovery from rewrites
description: Fixups currently rediscover safety facts inside each rewrite pass, then immediately mutate the Rust AST. As idiomatization grows, this duplicates brittle pattern matching for mutability/aliasing, ptr+len slice provenance, range bounds, and loop shape. Introduce a fact-discovery layer so passes can first compute conservative semantic facts, then later rewrite only when those facts are present. The intended model is phased: fact -> fixup -> recompute facts -> fixup, because each rewrite exposes simpler syntax and invalidates expression-level facts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixup infrastructure has an explicit fact-analysis entry point and fact context.
- Facts are keyed by stable semantic identities where possible, not traversal-only positions.
- Rewrites consume facts instead of recomputing their full proof locally.
- Phase ordering documents when facts are recomputed versus preserved through lineage.
- Mutability, ptr+len slice recovery, and lifted-slice loop recovery have concrete fact-backed migration tickets.
close_reason: Closed

Breakdown from regenerated crate: 34 'expected _unnamed_at_*, found integer' (struct/field init assigns an integer where a nested anonymous struct value is expected — likely zero-init of aggregate fields); ~20 function-pointer/opaque-pointer alias mismatches (Option<fn(...)> vs *mut u8, *mut () vs *mut c_void, *mut FILE vs *mut _IO_FILE); 7 residual 'expected *mut u8, found *mut i8' char cases q0g.4 did not cover; 2 'expected yaml_tag_directive_s, found integer'. Regenerate with the libyaml SLATE_CLANG_ARGS and recount.

close_reason: Implemented libyaml residual E0308 fixes: cached translate-project --lib frontend work, capped inline_temps on large ASTs, handled function-pointer typedef fields, void*/FILE record types, target-typed string global casts, and aggregate const-array parsing. Verified cargo nextest r --release and regenerated ~/libyaml with cargo r --release; generated crate cargo check --lib reports zero errors.

title: Model cfg attributes as rust_ast nodes, not strings
description: Why: translate-cfg currently renders each config to Rust text, splits it back into top-level items by brace/paren scanning, and splices #[cfg(...)] as a formatted string. This violates the project rule that the emitter builds structured AST, never rendered strings. What: add a structured rust_ast::Cfg predicate enum and an Item::Cfg wrapper, render them in codegen, have preprocess::pred_to_cfg build Cfg values, and rewrite the cfg_translate merge to operate on rust_ast Items so the #[cfg(...)] gate is emitted from the AST. Output must stay byte-for-byte identical.
close_reason: Added rust_ast::Cfg (Flag/Opt/Not/Any/All) + Item::Cfg wrapper, rendered by codegen. preprocess::pred_to_cfg now builds Cfg values (Branch.rust_cfg: Option<Cfg>); cfg_translate merges/gates whole rust_ast Items via item_key, dropping all text-splitting. #[cfg(...)] now emitted from the AST, not a formatted string. Output byte-for-byte unchanged; 196 tests pass.

title: Support printf hex and octal integer conversions
description: Why: %x, %X, and %o are common in C diagnostics and map cleanly to Rust format traits. What: extend constant printf parsing to recover supported hex and octal integer conversions as print!/println! placeholders, including mixed formats, while preserving all-or-nothing fallback for unsupported cases. Acceptance: add focused parser tests, fixture coverage, and differential output-shape assertions.
notes: touches: src/fixups/printf_format.rs, tests/differential.rs, tests/fixtures/printf_hex_octal.c

Added printf_hex_octal fixture and differential output-shape assertions. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release on main (196 passed).

title: Improve printf parsing for Rust macro recovery
description:
Why: slate-04q.8 adds a conservative all-or-nothing printf-to-print macro recovery pass for constant formats with plain text, %d, and %%. Broader printf support should be added incrementally without mixing Rust stdout macros with remaining libc printf calls in the same generated program.

What to do:
- Extend constant printf format parsing in focused, verified steps.
- Keep unsupported or ambiguous formats on the baseline unsafe extern path.
- Preserve the all-or-nothing per-program rule unless stdout buffering is unified another way.
- Add output-shape assertions and keep differential tests green.

title: Support signed integer width and length printf formats
description:
Why: many C fixtures and real programs use integer spellings beyond bare %d, such as %i, %ld, %lld, %u, %lu, %llu, and %zu. These can map to Rust formatting when argument typing is unambiguous.

What to do:
- Extend the constant-format parser for a conservative integer subset.
- Preserve exact argument counts and reject ambiguous width/length combinations.
- Keep mixed or unsupported programs on the baseline unsafe printf path.
- Add unit tests and differential output-shape coverage.
close_reason: Extended printf macro recovery to %i, %u, %ld, %lu, %lld, %llu, and %zu constant integer formats with exact argument counts. Added unit and differential output-shape coverage. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Rewrite string length/compare: strlen/strcmp/strncmp/memcmp
description:
Once a value is lifted to &str/&[u8]/String (slate-58r.1), rewrite:
- strlen(s) -> s.len()
- strcmp(a,b) == 0 -> a == b ; strcmp ordering -> a.cmp(b)
- strncmp(a,b,n) -> a[..n] compare (bounds-checked)
- memcmp(a,b,n) on lifted slices -> a == b (also usable via slate-58r.2)

Most common and most mechanical family -> highest priority. Keep raw libc call when operands are not lifted.
acceptance_criteria: - Lifted-operand calls render as len()/==/cmp/slice-compare; unlifted operands stay raw.\n- strcmp sign semantics preserved (==0 vs <0/>0 mapped to == / Ordering).\n- Differential fixtures cover equal, prefix, and ordering cases.
close_reason: Adjusted lifted strlen rewrites to keep Rust's native usize result: generated temps now use usize and assign s.len() directly instead of u64 plus as u64. Verified fixture output plus cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Substrate: lift char* / nul-terminated buffers to &str / String / &[u8]
description:
Analysis + lowering pass that recognizes when a C `char*` / `const char*` (and char-array locals) can be represented as a Rust `&str`, `String`, or `&[u8]` carrying an explicit length, instead of a bare `*const i8`/`*mut i8`.

This is THE highest-leverage prerequisite: it unlocks the entire str* / parse family (slen/compare/copy/search/parse rewrites). None of those can be done safely until a value is lifted, because a raw `*const i8` has no length and no UTF-8/nul guarantee.

Must preserve C semantics precisely: nul-termination boundary, non-UTF-8 bytes (prefer `&[u8]`/`CStr` when bytes aren't provably UTF-8), aliasing/mutation through the pointer, and pointer identity where later code does arithmetic on it. Where a value cannot be proven liftable, leave it as the raw pointer (correctness over idiom).

## Context
Gates slate-58r string-family rewrites. Broader than libc: also affects string-literal and char-array representation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Lowered code represents provably-liftable C strings as &str/String/&[u8] with a length, not raw *const i8.
- Non-UTF-8 / byte-buffer cases fall back to &[u8]/CStr, never lossy String.
- Values used in raw pointer arithmetic or passed to unlifted externs stay raw.
- Differential tests green; fixtures cover UTF-8, embedded-non-ASCII, and mutation-through-pointer cases.
close_reason: Implemented AST string_lift fixup with structural &str/&[u8] Rust AST types, conservative raw-pointer safety checks, and differential coverage. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Idiomatize libc calls into higher-level Rust forms
description:
Why: Slate currently lowers most C standard-library calls faithfully but unidiomatically -- they flow through the generic extern path (declared `unsafe extern "C"`, called through raw pointers / `libc`). Only the mem* family has dedicated handlers (src/lower.rs:1183). memchr (slate-04q.26) and printf->format-macro (slate-04q.8) are the only idiomatization tickets so far. This epic collects the rest.

Key architectural insight: the function-call rewrite is the EASY half. The hard, high-leverage prerequisite is a set of DATA-TYPE LIFTING passes that turn raw C representations into owned/borrowed Rust types carrying length and provenance:
- `char*` / nul-terminated buffers -> `&str` / `String` / `&[u8]`
- `(T*, len)` pairs -> `&[T]` / `Vec<T>`
- heap and resource handles (`malloc`/`free`, `FILE*`) -> `Box`/`Vec` / `std::fs`+`io`

Almost every str*/parse/sort/heap/stdio rewrite is nearly mechanical ONCE the underlying value is lifted, and cannot be done safely before it (e.g. `strlen(p)` can only become `s.len()` when `p` is a slice/str with a known length, not a bare `*const i8`). So children are split into (a) substrate lifting passes and (b) per-family call rewrites that depend on them.

Contrast with memchr: it is pointer-in/pointer-out, so it needed no type lift -- which is exactly why it was doable standalone. Most of this epic is not.

Correctness invariant (inherited from slate-04q): every idiomatization is a fixup; disabling it must still leave correct baseline Rust. Verify with differential tests + output-shape assertions.

## Context
Relates to the fixup epic slate-04q (shares the fixup module + correctness invariant). printf idiomatization is tracked separately as slate-04q.8; memchr as slate-04q.26 -- do not duplicate.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented set of type-lifting substrate passes exists (string, slice, heap/handle), each usable independently.
- Per-family libc call-rewrite fixups are gated on the relevant substrate and are individually optional-in-spirit.
- Every rewrite is covered by a differential fixture and an output-shape assertion.
- docs/idiomatization.md describes the lift->rewrite dependency and the pointer-provenance / nul-termination invariants each pass relies on.
- Priority ordering reflects ease x commonality: common+mechanical rewrites land before rare or ownership-heavy ones.

title: Port atomic lowering helpers to Rust AST expressions
description:
Why: atomic load/fetch/xchg/cmpxchg lowering still constructs AtomicN::from_ptr, fetch calls, unsafe blocks, fallback RMW statements, and combine expressions with formatted strings.

title: Port call lowering from formatted strings to Expr::Call
description:
Why: lower_call currently builds generic calls as one formatted string, hiding callee, arguments, casts, unsafe wrappers, and indirect unwraps from AST fixups.

What to do:
- Represent direct and indirect callees as Expr nodes.
- Represent extern/variadic/complex unsafe wrappers as Expr::Unsafe(Expr::Call).
- Represent per-argument extern casts as Expr::Cast where legal.
- Leave special ABI shims such as strtold and printf long double on a separate raw path if needed.

Function-pointer unwrap and extern argument casts preserve current output semantics.
