title: Port place and assignment helpers to structured Expr targets
description:
Why: stores, copies, member/element places, bitfields, and pointer derefs still construct assignment targets with format! strings. That keeps lvalue paths opaque and risks precedence bugs around casts/deref/indexing.

What to do:
- Change place_expr/place_or_deref/bitfield_place and element/member assignment paths to return Expr where possible.
- Extend Stmt::Assign helper APIs to accept Expr targets instead of only strings.
- Port lower_store/lower_copy/bitfield get/set over to structured targets.
- Keep genuinely opaque raw pointer fallbacks isolated.
acceptance_criteria: Member, element, slot, global, and deref assignment targets are represented as Expr nodes on normal paths.\nString target formatting is restricted to opaque fallback cases.\ncargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented structured Expr targets for places and assignments in lower_store, lower_copy, member/element pointer tracking, and bitfield get/set. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Eliminate remaining raw Rust emission bridges
description:
Why: Slate is migrating generated Rust from raw formatted strings to rust_ast nodes so fixups can inspect, substitute, and preserve precedence. slate-04q.18 handled a first expression slice, but lower.rs still contains Val::expr/materialize(String)/emit_expr/emit_line and item/type raw formatting bridges.

What to do:
- Track the remaining raw/format bridge groups as focused child tasks.
- Prefer AST node additions or structured helper APIs over larger string helpers.
- Keep each child small enough for independent agents and verify with fmt plus release nextest gates.
- The end state should make Expr::Raw/Stmt::Raw/Item::Raw true escape hatches rather than normal emission paths.
acceptance_criteria: Focused child tasks exist for the remaining bridge groups.\nEach child removes a measurable class of raw/format emission.\nFinal cleanup can delete or tightly restrict Val::expr/materialize(String)/emit_expr raw helpers.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower to a structured Rust AST instead of Item::Raw text
description:
Foundational cross-cutting change enabling all AST-based fixups. Do NOT wire hard bd blockers: this is done solo (no parallel agents) because it touches the whole lowerer.

Current state: the pipeline is already three-phase in shape (lower::lower -> Program, fixups::apply(Program) -> Program, Program::emit -> String; see main.rs:74-83), BUT lower.rs builds every function/global/record as Item::Raw(String) of pre-rendered Rust. So the 'AST' is a bag of strings: fixups munge text (src/fixups/mod.rs) and emit() just concatenates.

Goal: make lower() populate the REAL structured nodes already defined in src/rust_ast.rs (Func/Param/Block/Stmt/Expr/Type, with Raw escape hatches on Item and Expr). Then the three steps become meaningful: (1) build AST, (2) transform AST (fixups as Program->Program passes), (3) emit AST->string as the final step before writing files.

Scope of the migration:
- Expression layer: replace Val::Expr(String) with Val::Expr(rust_ast::Expr); build Binary/Unary/Cast/Compare/Call/Ref/Deref nodes instead of format! fragments. Use Expr::Raw as the bridge for constructs not yet modeled so the migration is incremental and stays byte-safe.
- Statement layer: replace self.out: String / emit_line(&str) with a Vec<Stmt>; let/assign/return/while/expr become Stmt nodes. Control-flow text stays via Stmt::Raw / new nodes as needed.
- Precedence-aware rendering: give Expr::render precedence context so redundant parens are simply never emitted (this delivers slate-04q.12 for free; baseline stays correct because extra parens are always safe).

Enables/precedes the AST-dependent fixups (reimplemented as AST passes, not text): slate-04q.12 (paren elision), slate-04q.11 (unnecessary mut), slate-04q.7 (arg temp inlining), slate-04q.3/.4/.5 (compound-assign / temp / retval cleanups). No hard deps recorded per instruction.

Verify: cargo nextest r --release stays fully green at every step (differential suite is the safety net); cargo fmt.
notes: touches: src/lower.rs (Val, materialize, emit_line, lower_func, expr constructors), src/rust_ast.rs (precedence rendering, Stmt::Raw), src/fixups/mod.rs (port to AST passes). Worktree: ../slate-04q.13
close_reason: Lowerer now builds structured rust_ast Expr/Stmt nodes (Val::Expr(Expr), Vec<IndentStmt> body, precedence-aware render). Merged to main. Remaining raw bridges tracked in slate-04q.15.

title: Record preprocessor conditional regions for cfg recovery
description:
Why: CIR and the normal Clang AST only contain the active preprocessed branch. To recover portable cfgs, Slate needs a preprocessing oracle that records conditional directives, predicates, source ranges, and whether each branch was active.

What to do:
- Extend the frontend path to collect #if/#ifdef/#ifndef/#elif/#else/#endif regions before CIR lowering.
- Preserve normalized predicate text and source ranges that can be joined to AST declarations and lowered Rust items.
- Track active versus inactive branches for the current invocation.
- Start with predicates used by tests/fixtures.cfg: _WIN32, __linux__, __APPLE__, architecture macros, and NDEBUG.

Out of scope: evaluating arbitrary project macro expressions beyond recording and simple known-predicate normalization.
acceptance_criteria:
Preprocessing metadata is available to later pipeline stages.
The cfg fixture predicates are recorded with source ranges and active/inactive state.
Unknown predicates are preserved as diagnostics/opaque expressions rather than guessed.
Existing single-config translation behavior is unchanged.
close_reason: Added preprocessing oracle (src/preprocess.rs) recording #if/#ifdef/#ifndef/#elif/#else/#endif regions with normalized predicates, directive/body source ranges, mapped Rust cfgs, and active/inactive state resolved against Clang's predefined macros. Unknown predicates are kept opaque + diagnosed, not guessed. Exposed via 'record-cfg' JSON command; recorded cfgs match tests/fixtures.cfg/expected_cfgs.json. Existing single-config/translate-cfg behavior unchanged. Verified with cargo nextest r --release (183 tests).

title: Run a bounded multi-config Clang/CIR matrix
description:
Why: disabled preprocessor branches cannot produce AST or CIR in a single Clang invocation. Slate needs a bounded multi-config mode that invokes the existing CIR pipeline for selected target/debug configurations.

What to do:
- Add a frontend mode that accepts or constructs a small configuration matrix.
- Include initial built-in configs covering Windows, Linux, Apple, x86_64, Arm/AArch64, debug, and NDEBUG-style release.
- Run each config through the existing emit-cir/parse/lower path and retain the predicate/config identity for each result.
- Cache or de-duplicate identical configs/results where practical.

Out of scope: exhaustive combinatorial exploration of arbitrary project macros.
acceptance_criteria:
The cfg fixtures can be translated under the relevant built-in or supplied configurations.
Each translated variant is tagged with the configuration/predicate that produced it.
Invalid or unsupported config variants fail with targeted diagnostics.
Existing single-config commands continue to work.
close_reason: Added experimental translate-cfg command with built-in OS, architecture, and NDEBUG macro config matrices. Variants run through existing CIR/AST/lower/fixup path, merge same-named whole functions for the fixture shape, and are verified by cfg fixture shape plus compile tests. Verified with cargo nextest r --release.

title: Merge whole-item cfg variants in the Rust emitter
description:
Why: after multiple config-specific CIR lowerings, Slate needs to stitch compatible Rust items into one portable Rust module guarded by cfg attributes. Whole items are the first tractable merge unit.

What to do:
- Identify matching source items across variants by source location, symbol name, and item kind.
- Emit #[cfg(...)] attributes for whole functions/globals/types when variants map cleanly to known Rust cfg predicates.
- Support alternate bodies for the same function name and cfg-exclusive items.
- Refuse expression-fragment or syntax-fragment macro cuts with diagnostics.

Out of scope: merging arbitrary statement/expression fragments.
acceptance_criteria:
OS, architecture, and NDEBUG fixture variants can emit whole-item Rust cfg attrs according to expected_cfgs.json.
Conflicting variants that cannot be represented as whole Rust items are diagnosed.
Single-config output remains unchanged unless multi-config mode is selected.
close_reason: Rewrote translate-cfg to derive the whole-item cfg matrix from the lq0.2 preprocessing oracle instead of a filename table: each recorded branch -> a variant with clang args pinning every chain macro, rust_cfg from the recorded predicate mapping, validated against the oracle to activate exactly its branch. OS/arch/NDEBUG fixture output is unchanged. Refuses with diagnostics: fragment cuts inside a function/record body (brace-depth scan), predicates without a known cfg mapping, and >1 top-level chain (nested/sibling deferred). No-conditional sources pass through to single-config lowering (unchanged). Known limitation: negated/ifndef opening branches are validation-refused rather than merged (candidate uses a define-atoms heuristic); multi/nested chains deferred per epic scope. Added reject fixtures + tests. Verified cargo nextest r --release (195 tests) and cargo fmt.

title: Add preprocessor cfg matrix fixtures
description:
Why: before implementing multi-config cfg recovery, Slate needs small C fixtures that exercise the macro predicates we want to recognize and preserve: Windows, Linux, Apple, x86_64, Arm, and NDEBUG. These fixtures should describe the intended semantic surface without requiring the new frontend mode to exist yet.

What to do:
- Add fixture sources under a dedicated test fixture area for future preprocessor/multi-config tests.
- Cover whole-item conditional compilation for _WIN32, __linux__, __APPLE__, architecture macros (__x86_64__, __aarch64__/__arm__), and NDEBUG.
- Include expected Rust cfg intent in checked metadata so future implementation tests have a stable target.
- Do not wire these fixtures into the existing generated differential test yet; that test only has single-config semantics today.
acceptance_criteria:
Checked fixtures exist for OS, architecture, and NDEBUG-style predicates.
Fixtures are isolated from the current generated differential harness until multi-config support exists.
Expected cfg mappings are documented next to the fixtures.
No production lowering behavior changes in this ticket.
close_reason: Added isolated tests/fixtures.cfg sources and expected cfg metadata for OS, architecture, and NDEBUG predicates. Verified JSON parsing and clang syntax checks.

title: Recover target/debug preprocessor configurations as Rust cfgs
description:
Why: Slate currently translates one preprocessed Clang/CIR view of a C file. Conditional compilation means untaken #if/#ifdef branches are absent from AST/CIR, so generated Rust is faithful only to the selected target/configuration, not to portable source that uses target/debug macro gates.

What to do:
- Add a multi-configuration frontend mode that records preprocessor conditional regions and runs Clang/CIR for a bounded set of meaningful configurations.
- Start with classic target/debug predicates: _WIN32, __linux__, __APPLE__, __x86_64__, __aarch64__/__arm__, and NDEBUG.
- Merge observed whole-item variants into Rust guarded by #[cfg(...)] where the source identity and predicate mapping are clean.
- Require user-supplied config sets for project-specific macro soup instead of guessing arbitrary combinations.
- Diagnose conditional regions that are not covered by any configured variant.

Out of scope initially: expression-fragment macro surgery, arbitrary combinatorial macro exploration, and translating inactive branches from a single Clang invocation.
acceptance_criteria:
Fixtures cover the initial target/debug macro predicates.
Frontend design records enough preprocessing information to map covered predicates to Rust cfgs.
The multi-config mode can lower observed variants through the existing CIR path and merge whole items behind cfg attrs.
Unsupported or uncovered conditional regions produce diagnostics rather than guessed Rust.
Documentation describes single-config versus multi-config portability semantics.
close_reason: All 8 children complete: cfg matrix fixtures, recorded conditional regions, bounded multi-config matrix, whole-item cfg merge, docs, uncovered/unmapped diagnostics, emit-fixtures cfg output, and cfg-as-rust_ast nodes.

title: Fuse local zero-init plus first assignment
description:
Why: baseline lowering initializes C locals to a zero value, then emits the first CIR store separately. In add.c this produces let mut c: i32 = 0; followed by c = ((a) + (b)); even though the first assignment can become the Rust initializer.

What to do:
- Recognize local declarations whose initializer is an artificial zero/default value and whose first read is preceded by exactly one dominating assignment.
- Rewrite let mut x: T = 0; ... x = expr; to let mut x: T = expr; when no read, address-take, volatile access, or aliasing-sensitive operation observes the placeholder value.
- Keep complex control flow, pointers, volatile locals, and address-taken locals on the baseline path until the analysis is explicit.
- This is the concrete dead-let/first-assignment cleanup exposed by add.c.
acceptance_criteria:
add.c generated Rust initializes c directly from a + b rather than zero-initializing and assigning separately.
Address-taken, volatile, and control-flow-ambiguous locals are left unchanged.
Differential tests stay green.
cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Added fuse_zero_init fixup: folds 'let mut x: T = 0; x = expr;' into 'let mut x: T = expr;' when the store is the immediately following line and does not read x. add.c now initializes c directly from a+b. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release (fixups unit tests + full differential suite green; cfg_translate failures are another agent's in-flight work in the coordination checkout, unrelated).

title: Collapse non-main retval boilerplate in fixups
description:
Why: helper functions currently lower C returns as __retval = value; return __retval;. Existing slate-04q.5 only covers main-specific store/load/process::exit cleanup, so ordinary function return boilerplate remains in fixtures such as add.c.

What to do:
- Recognize simple non-main patterns like __retval = expr; return __retval;.
- Rewrite to return expr; without changing control flow.
- Optionally fold final return expr; into a Rust tail expression only when it is the final statement in the function/block and type behavior is unchanged.
- Keep multiple-return and control-flow-heavy cases on the baseline path until proven.
- Add output-shape coverage using add.c or a focused return fixture.
acceptance_criteria:
add.c helper add no longer emits __retval = c; return __retval;.
Multiple-return and conditional-return fixtures continue to compile and behave correctly.
The fixup is optional in spirit; baseline lowering remains correct without it.
Differential tests stay green.
cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented collapse_retval fixup: folds '__retval = expr; return __retval;' into 'return expr;' and drops the slot decl when the slot is assigned exactly once immediately before the return and mentioned nowhere else. Runs after temp inlining so the pattern is canonical. main (process::exit) is naturally excluded. add.c helper now emits 'return c;'. Added 4 unit tests. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release (132 passed).

title: Recover simple printf calls as Rust format macros
description:
Why: generated Rust still emits unsafe extern printf calls for constant format strings such as printf("%d\n", add(2, 3)). That is correct baseline lowering, but it keeps unsafe/libc in the common easy case where Rust formatting can express the same output.

What to do:
- Recognize printf calls with a constant C string format argument.
- Start with the strict add.c shape: %d followed by newline and one integer argument, emitted as println!("{}", arg).
- Preserve fallback to unsafe printf for dynamic formats, unsupported specifiers, locale-sensitive behavior, or ambiguous argument typing.
- Remove the now-unused printf extern declaration only when no printf calls remain.
- Add output-shape assertions and keep differential tests green.
acceptance_criteria:
add.c generated Rust uses println! for the three printf("%d\n", ...) calls.
Unsupported printf formats remain on the baseline unsafe extern path.
The printf extern declaration is removed when all printf uses are rewritten.
Differential tests stay green.
cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented AST printf format recovery for constant formats with plain text, %%, and one or more %d conversions; all-or-nothing per program to avoid mixed stdout buffering; removes printf extern when fully rewritten. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Eliminate parameter spill prologue in fixups
description:
Why: CIR faithfully spills every C parameter into an alloca + store because C params are mutable lvalues, so baseline lowering emits `let mut a: i32 = 0; ... a = arg0;` for each parameter. This is correct but noisy; the parameter binding can absorb the local directly.

What to do:
- Recognize, per parameter argK: exactly one local decl `let mut NAME: T = 0;`, exactly one store `NAME = argK;`, argK used nowhere else, and local type T equal to the param type.
- Rewrite the signature to bind the parameter under the local name, keeping mut (e.g. `fn add(mut a: i32, mut b: i32)`), and delete both the local decl and the spill store.
- Keeping mut in the signature preserves correctness when the C body reassigns the parameter. Address-of the parameter still refers to a real place.

Guards:
- Skip if NAME collides with another parameter name or another param renames to the same NAME.
- Skip if argK is used more than once (not a pure spill) or if the local type does not match the param type.
- This is a fixup: disabling it must still leave correct baseline Rust.

## Context
First of two fixups from add.c review. Low risk, independent of others, string-based rewrite is sufficient (type annotation just moves to the signature, no inference risk). Do this before the call-argument inlining fixup.
acceptance_criteria:
add.c generated Rust binds params under source names (fn add(mut a: i32, mut b: i32)) with no spill decls/stores.
Params reassigned in the C body still compile and behave correctly.
Address-taken parameters still work.
Differential tests stay green.
cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented eliminate_param_spills fixup: folds the CIR parameter-spill prologue (let mut a=0; a=arg0;) into direct 'fn f(mut a: T, ...)' bindings when the slot is only seeded from its param and not read before the spill. String-based, keeps mut for later reassignment. Added 5 unit tests. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release (128 passed).

title: Improve stdlib test compilation performance
description: Stdlib coverage has grown large enough that test runtime is dominated by compiling many tiny generated Rust programs and matching C probes. tests/support::compare_batch already builds all generated Rust programs in one Cargo invocation under src/bin, but build_batch currently removes the whole batch project, including Cargo target artifacts, before every run. First investigate the minimal fix: preserve the batch Cargo target directory across runs and write generated/bin sources only when their contents actually change, so Cargo can reuse unchanged dependency and bin artifacts. If that is not enough, investigate a larger harness shape such as an aggregate Rust runner/module graph that dispatches per case. Preserve differential behavior, per-probe diagnostics, stdin/argv/env handling, stderr comparison, exit-code comparison, and fallback/error reporting for compile failures.
acceptance_criteria: stdlib_coverage repeat-run runtime is measurably reduced on the current corpus; unchanged generated Rust probes reuse Cargo artifacts where feasible; generated files are not rewritten unnecessarily; per-probe pass/fail output and known-unsupported ratchet behavior are preserved; harness comments explain cache invalidation and how to force a clean rebuild/debug an individual compile failure.
notes: Implemented local harness changes: preserve tests/support batch_cargo target artifacts, write generated/batch files only when bytes differ, and isolate KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED stdlib probes so expected compile failures do not force per-case fallback for all passing probes. Timing on this machine: clean target/stdlib-coverage cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture dropped from ~90s baseline to 21.32s real; immediate warm repeat was 17.90s real; cargo nextest r --release --test stdlib_coverage passed in 11.816s warm.
close_reason: Implemented stdlib coverage batch-cache improvements: preserved batch Cargo target artifacts, avoided rewriting unchanged generated sources, and isolated known-unsupported probes from passing batch builds. Verified with cargo nextest r --release --test stdlib_coverage.

title: Emit libc:: path for opaque pthread/libc struct types (pthread_t, pthread_attr_t)
description: A multithreaded C program (pthread_create/join over an atomic global) now translates with no unsupported-op warnings and the atomic ops lower correctly (AtomicI32::from_ptr...fetch_add). But the generated Rust references bare type names like 'pthread_attr_t' and 'pthread_t' (e.g. '_v6 as *mut pthread_attr_t') instead of 'libc::pthread_attr_t', so it fails to compile (E0425). Slate should resolve opaque libc struct types to their libc:: path (or emit an extern type). This blocks adding a deterministic multithreaded differential fixture (4 threads x 100000 atomic_fetch_add == 400000) that would prove atomic thread-safety end to end.
acceptance_criteria: tests/fixtures/mt-atomics.c (pthread + atomic_fetch_add) translates AND the generated Rust compiles and passes differential (prints 400000).
close_reason: Implemented libc pthread type mapping in baseline lowering and added mt-atomics differential fixture plus emitted-path regression test. Verified before merge with cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release --test differential pthread_opaque_types_use_libc_paths --no-capture, cargo nextest r --release --test differential generated_differential --no-capture, and cargo nextest r --release (415 passed).

title: Lower CIR libm and math builtin ops
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks the CIR math builtin/libm op set as P2 unsupported. These ops broaden stdlib/math coverage without blocking core scalar C.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for CIR math ops listed under math builtins/libm in docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
- Map to Rust inherent methods, libm/libc calls, or runtime helpers as appropriate for C-compatible behavior.
- Add fixtures for representative unary, binary, rounding, min/max, and fmod/pow cases before expanding the full set.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md as each op lands.
close_reason: Implemented direct lowering for CIR math builtin/libm ops to Rust float methods, float remainder, and integer casts for rounding ops; added synthetic lowerer coverage for the direct op spellings, added math_builtin_ops differential fixture for frontend-emitted libm calls, and updated docs/cir-op-prioritization.md. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo fmt, cargo run -- emit-fixtures, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Lower CIR integer bit builtin ops
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.bit_reverse, cir.byte_swap, cir.clrsb, cir.clz, cir.ctz, cir.ffs, cir.parity, cir.popcount, and cir.rotate as P2 unsupported. These builtins are common in optimized C and systems code.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for the integer bit builtin op family.
- Map to Rust integer methods where semantics match, with helpers for C-specific edge cases such as zero inputs where required.
- Add differential fixtures covering widths, signedness, zero inputs, and rotate counts.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Implemented direct lowering for CIR integer bit builtin ops: bitreverse, byte_swap, clrsb, clz, ctz, ffs, parity, popcount, and rotate. Added synthetic lowerer tests for direct op spellings and C-specific ffs/clrsb semantics, added integer_bit_builtin_ops differential fixture covering unsigned/signed/zero/rotate cases, and updated docs/cir-op-prioritization.md. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo fmt, cargo run -- emit-fixtures, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Lower CIR constant and object-size query ops
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.is_constant and cir.objsize as P2 unsupported. These show up in builtin probing and optimized libc/header code.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for cir.is_constant and cir.objsize.
- Preserve observable C builtin behavior for common compile-time and object-size queries.
- Add stdlib/header probes or differential fixtures that exercise both known and unknown object sizes.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Implemented direct cir.is_constant and cir.objsize lowering with E2E fixture coverage

title: Document CIR op checklist update rule in workflow
description:
Why: Agents adding support for a new CIR op need to update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md at the same time, otherwise the unsupported inventory drifts.

What to do:
- Add a note to WORKFLOW.md that new CIR op support must mark the op complete in docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
- Keep the note near work selection or handoff guidance so agents see it before implementation.
notes: touches: WORKFLOW.md
close_reason: Added WORKFLOW.md note requiring docs/cir-op-prioritization.md updates when adding CIR op support.

title: Introduce fixup module boundary for CIR-to-Rust cleanups
description:
Why: Cleanup logic should not make src/lower.rs harder to reason about. The lowerer/visitor should emit faithful baseline Rust from CIR; a new fixup directory/module should own readability rewrites.

What to do:
- Add a new fixup module/directory, for example src/fixups/ or src/rust_fixups/.
- Define a small pass entry point that accepts the lowered representation and returns rewritten Rust output/AST.
- Wire the translate path so baseline lowering remains explicit and fixups run afterward.
- Keep pass scheduling simple and fixed; do not add configurable pass machinery yet.
- Update docs/passes.md and docs/idiomatization.md with the new boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixup code lives outside the baseline lowerer visitor.
- The existing visitor remains responsible for emitting correct baseline code, not readability rewrites.
- translate and emit-fixtures still work.
- cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented src/fixups apply boundary and wired translate/translate-project through it; documented the post-lower fixup stage. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Add CIR-driven pure temp inlining fixup
description:
Why: Generated Rust currently materializes every CIR SSA result as a Rust temporary, producing much larger code than the source for simple expressions.

What to do:
- Recognize single-use pure temps produced from constants, simple local loads, arithmetic, casts, and other side-effect-free CIR expressions.
- Inline those temps into their use sites when there is no intervening store, call, volatile access, or aliasing hazard.
- Preserve explicit source locals from cir.alloca names; only eliminate synthetic value temps.
- Leave ambiguous cases on the baseline path.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/fixtures/compound_assignments.c output no longer contains one let per constant/load/binop in the simple assignment chains.
- Volatile and call-side-effect cases are not inlined unsafely.
- Differential tests stay green.
- cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented conservative single-use temp inlining in src/fixups with barriers for calls, method receivers, volatile/pointer intrinsics, and side-effecting statements. Added fixture output-shape coverage for compound_assignments. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release after merge.

title: Recover compound assignment from CIR load-binop-store patterns
description:
Why: CIR lowers compound assignments like a -= 5 into load a, binop, store a. The Rust fixup should prefer compound assignment syntax when that pattern is safe, even though CIR alone cannot distinguish original a -= 5 from a = a - 5.

What to do:
- Match store(binop(load(ptr), rhs), ptr) for simple local slots.
- Emit compound assignment by project preference: +=, -=, *=, /=, %=, <<=, >>=, &=, ^=, |=.
- Require rhs to be pure and safe to inline.
- Exclude volatile accesses and complex lvalues until their safety rules are explicit.
- Add output-shape coverage using tests/fixtures/compound_assignments.c.
acceptance_criteria:
- compound_assignments generated Rust uses compound assignment for the simple local updates.
- The pass documents the preference for compound assignment when CIR admits multiple equivalent source spellings.
- Differential tests stay green.
- cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented compound_assign fixup: rewrites 'a = a <op> rhs' -> 'a <op>= rhs' for simple local slots with pure rhs. Added Stmt::CompoundAssign to Rust AST. Verified with cargo fmt + cargo nextest r --release (136 passed).

title: Add CIR-to-Rust fixup pass pipeline
description:
Why: Slate's current lowerer emits correct but very temp-heavy Rust by materializing every CIR SSA value as a Rust let. Readability cleanup should be a fixup layer on the CIR-to-Rust side, not additional responsibility inside the visitor that emits baseline Rust.

What to do:
- Add a dedicated source directory/module for Rust cleanup fixups that operate on lowered CIR/Rust structure.
- Keep the existing CIR visitor focused on faithful code emission.
- Make fixups optional in spirit: disabling them still leaves correct baseline Rust.
- Prefer compact Rust forms such as compound assignment when CIR admits multiple source spellings.
- Verify every fixup with differential tests and output-shape assertions where stable.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented fixup module/directory exists separate from the baseline lowerer visitor.
- The pipeline clearly runs baseline lowering first, then optional cleanup fixups.
- Initial cleanup tickets cover compound assignment, pure temp inlining, unused call-result cleanup, and main retval collapse.
- docs/passes.md or docs/idiomatization.md describes the boundary between emission and fixups.

title: Model external libc struct types (struct tm, struct lconv)
description: Probes calling gmtime/mktime/asctime/strftime and localeconv fail to build: Slate references the opaque libc struct type (e.g. 'tm', 'lconv') as a Rust type but never emits a definition, member access through a pointer to it yields 'unsupported get_member base' (falls back to '*(_0)'), and a local 'struct tm t = {0}' references an unemitted '__const.main.t'. Need to model external/opaque struct layouts (via Clang AST record facts) so their fields can be read/written and the type exists in Rust. Surfaced by tests/stdlib/time/* and tests/stdlib/locale/localeconv.
close_reason: Implemented standard libc record definitions/defaults for struct tm and struct lconv, zero aggregate record init, and member access through loaded record pointers. Promoted localeconv/asctime/gmtime/mktime/strftime stdlib probes. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture, and cargo test.

title: Lower address-of array element (&arr[i])
description: Taking the address of an array element via &arr[i] lowers to a placeholder identifier instead of a pointer. 'int *p = &arr[1];' emits 'p = _;' (and 'p = _1;' for further uses), producing Rust that does not compile. The array-subscript place is computed (index _vN) but the address-of does not form '(&mut arr[i]) as *mut T'. Blocks pointer-difference / pointer-into-array programs. Discovered by tests/stdlib/stddef/ptrdiff.c (currently in KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED under slate-nk3.11).
acceptance_criteria: tests/stdlib/stddef/ptrdiff.c passes stdlib_coverage and can be promoted out of KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED; &arr[i] lowers to a valid raw pointer.
close_reason: Implemented pointer rendering for recorded member/element places so &arr[i] lowers to std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(arr[(i) as usize]). Added tests/fixtures/address_of_array_element.c and promoted stddef/ptrdiff out of KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED. Verified with cargo test --test differential generated_differential -- --nocapture address_of_array_element, cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture, cargo run -- emit-fixtures, and cargo fmt && cargo test before and after merge.

title: Document multi-worktree beads workflow
description: Add WORKFLOW.md explaining how multiple agents should select beads, avoid linked in-progress tickets, use git worktrees, and integrate branches with minimal merge conflicts. Link it from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: Added WORKFLOW.md with multi-agent worktree and linked-bead selection rules. Linked it from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. Verified by inspecting the markdown and git diff.

title: Cross-TU globals: resolve extern globals to sibling module imports
description: Follow-up to slate-5mo (cross-TU function imports). translate-project currently wires only functions across translation units; a global declared 'extern int counter;' in one unit and defined 'int counter = 0;' in another still lowers the extern side to a body-less 'static mut' in an 'unsafe extern C' block instead of importing the sibling's definition. What to do: in translate-project pass 1 also collect defined globals (cir.global with an initial_value / non-extern) per module; in lower_with_project, when an extern_global's symbol is defined in a sibling module, emit 'use crate::<mod>::<sym>;' and make the defining module emit the static as 'pub static mut'. Add a differential fixture under tests/fixtures.multi (e.g. a shared counter incremented across units) and assert the extern global becomes a module import, not an extern C decl. One fixture, no fuzzing.
design: Mirror the function path: extend ProjectInfo with a cross_module_globals map (sym->module); reuse the existing extern_globals collection point in lower.rs to divert sibling-defined globals to cross_uses. Defining module marks the static pub (gate on emit_pub). Keep C-side well-defined (no UB); both sides must agree on init order.
close_reason: Implemented cross-TU globals. ProjectInfo.cross_module_globals (global sym->module) diverts extern globals to 'use crate::<mod>::<sym>;'; defining module emits 'pub static mut'. lower::defined_globals() lists initialized globals; translate-project pass 1 collects them. Fixture tests/fixtures.multi/globals/{main,state}.c (shared counter read+written across units); both print 8, exit 0. Test cross_tu_globals asserts import (not extern static) + pub static. cargo fmt + full suite green.

title: Cross-TU translation: multi-file project preserved as Rust modules
description: Real C splits across translation units. Add a translate-project mode that translates a directory of .c files into separate Rust module files that import each other (mod + use crate::m::sym), rather than aggregating into one file. A body-less prototype resolving to a sibling TU becomes a module import instead of an extern C decl; defined functions emit pub. Differential test compiles all .c together and all .rs as one crate, comparing stdout+exit. One fixture, no fuzzing.
close_reason: Implemented translate-project: dir of .c files -> separate Rust modules with mod/use crate wiring (not aggregated). Cross-TU prototypes resolve to sibling module imports; defined fns emit pub. Test tests/cross_tu.rs + fixtures.multi/cross_tu/{main,math}.c; C linked together and Rust built as one crate both print '36 64', exit 0. cargo fmt + full test suite pass. Functions only; globals cross-TU is follow-up.

title: Support function prototypes and declarations without bodies
description:
Why: Real C separates declarations from definitions and uses header-origin prototypes. Slate has extern libc declarations in limited cases, but user prototypes and body-less declarations need first-class handling.

What to do:
- Add fixtures for user prototypes before definitions, mutually-referenced functions where possible, body-less extern declarations, and header-origin declarations used by calls.
- Extend c_ast.rs/lower.rs to preserve and emit function signatures consistently.
- Avoid duplicate Rust item emission when a declaration and definition share the same symbol.
- Keep cross-translation-unit support scoped to declarations visible to the single input being translated.
acceptance_criteria:
- Differential fixtures cover prototypes before definitions and extern body-less declarations.
- Duplicate declarations do not produce duplicate Rust functions.
- Calls use the declared signature for casts/ABI decisions.
- cargo fmt and cargo test pass.
close_reason: CIR already merges prototype-before-definition into the single definition op (no duplicate emission), and body-less user declarations already flow through the extern "C" collection with correct signatures/casts. Added guarding differential fixtures: function_prototypes.c (fwd decl + mutual recursion + out-of-order defs) and extern_decl.c (body-less libc externs). No lower.rs/c_ast.rs changes needed. cargo fmt + full cargo test pass.

title: Broaden global variable support
description:
Why: Slate currently supports only a narrow set of file-scope static primitive globals and constant strings used by printf. Real C needs external globals, non-static globals, aggregate globals, and richer constant initializers.

What to do:
- Add fixtures for non-static definitions, extern declarations, primitive globals without explicit initializers, aggregate globals, and global loads/stores across functions.
- Extend global collection and extern declaration emission in lower.rs.
- Preserve C zero-initialization and mutability semantics conservatively with static mut where needed.
- Update docs/README.md and c.bnf as support lands.
acceptance_criteria:
- Differential fixtures cover primitive, aggregate, zero-initialized, extern, and cross-function global access cases.
- Generated Rust compiles and links for covered extern/global forms.
- Existing static global fixtures still pass.
- cargo fmt and cargo test pass.
close_reason: Broadened global lowering for non-static, zero-initialized, array, and struct globals; added global_vars differential coverage and updated docs/c.bnf. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo test.

title: Broaden aggregate type and initializer coverage
description:
Why: Slate handles simple structs, unions, and fixed-size primitive arrays, but real C uses nested aggregates, arrays of structs, struct assignment, and richer initializer forms.

What to do:
- Add fixtures for nested structs/unions, arrays of structs, structs containing arrays, aggregate assignment/copy, designated initializers if CIR/AST retain enough information, and partial initializers.
- Extend c_ast.rs type extraction as needed for nested aggregate facts.
- Extend lower.rs aggregate copy/init paths while keeping baseline Rust layout-compatible.
- Update docs and fuzzer coverage incrementally.
acceptance_criteria:
- Differential fixtures cover nested aggregates, arrays of structs, struct-with-array fields, aggregate copy, and partial init.
- Generated Rust uses layout-compatible #[repr(C)] types.
- Unsupported initializer forms produce explicit diagnostics until covered.
- cargo fmt and cargo test pass.
close_reason: Broadened aggregate coverage: nested structs/unions, arrays of structs, struct-with-array, aggregate copy, and nested/partial/designated/union initializers now lower and pass differential tests. place_expr composes member/element places; render_const_value renders const_record/const_array recursively. Fixtures added. Follow-up slate-kkt for union array-member unsafe wrapping.

title: Implement source break and continue lowering
description:
Why: C break and continue are unsupported even though Slate lowers for/while loops. Real loop bodies need early exit and skip-to-next-iteration control flow.

What to do:
- Add fixtures for break in while/for, continue in while/for, nested loops, and break inside switch once switch exists.
- Inspect CIR shapes for cir.break/cir.continue or block terminators.
- Add lowerer support that maps simple loop-local cases to Rust break/continue.
- For nonlocal/nested CFG shapes, coordinate with the dispatch-loop path used by goto/switch work.
- Update c.bnf and docs/README.md when supported.
acceptance_criteria:
- Differential fixtures cover break, continue, nested loops, and interactions with if.
- Simple cases emit ordinary Rust break/continue.
- Existing loop fixtures still pass.
- cargo fmt and cargo test pass.
close_reason: Implemented break/continue lowering for for/while loops incl. labeled-block continue for for-step semantics; fixtures + fuzzer + grammar + docs updated

title: Expand C operator coverage
description:
Why: The supported subset still lacks common operators: logical &&/||/!, many bitwise cases, assignment operators beyond +=, unary negation, and broader explicit casts. This blocks many ordinary expressions.

What to do:
- Add fixtures for logical short-circuiting, unary logical not, unary arithmetic negation, bitwise operations, compound assignments, and explicit casts across supported scalar types.
- Inspect CIR shapes and add lowerer handlers or extend existing handlers.
- Preserve C short-circuit semantics for && and ||.
- Extend the fuzzer and c.bnf only after each operator class is supported.
acceptance_criteria:
- Differential fixtures cover each newly supported operator class.
- Logical && and || are verified to short-circuit.
- Generated Rust compiles without todo! fallbacks for covered operators.
- cargo fmt and cargo test pass.
close_reason: Implemented unary negation lowering for cir.minus/cir.fneg, hardened operator rendering around casts, added differential fixtures for logical short-circuiting, unary !/-, compound assignments, and explicit casts, and expanded cgen/c.bnf/docs operator coverage. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Complete nonlocal and selection control flow
description:
Why: Slate supports structured if/for/while, but C programs rely on switch, break, continue, and goto-like nonlocal control flow. goto has a dedicated bead already, but the surrounding control-flow surface needs tracked work so the supported subset can grow coherently.

What to do:
- Add baseline lowering for switch statements.
- Add source-level break and continue in loops and switch contexts.
- Keep structured control flow structured when possible.
- Use conservative dispatch/state-machine lowering only when the CIR shape requires it.
- Extend fixtures, fuzzer surface, docs/README.md, and c.bnf as each construct becomes supported.
acceptance_criteria: - Child control-flow beads pass their differential fixtures.\n- Existing if/for/while fixtures still lower through the structured path where possible.\n- docs/README.md and c.bnf reflect the newly supported control-flow constructs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Implement C switch lowering
description:
Why: switch is listed as unsupported and is common in real C programs. CIR is expected to retain switch-level structure, so baseline lowering should preserve semantics before any idiomatic cleanup.

What to do:
- Add C fixtures for dense cases, sparse cases, default-only behavior, fallthrough, and switch without default.
- Inspect actual CIR with cargo run -- emit-cir.
- Add parser/lowerer support for the emitted cir.switch shape and any required terminators.
- Lower conservatively to Rust match/loop/dispatch form as needed to preserve C fallthrough.
- Update c.bnf and docs/README.md when supported.
acceptance_criteria:
- Differential fixtures cover default, no-default, fallthrough, and multiple case labels.
- cargo run -- translate succeeds for switch fixtures.
- cargo test --test differential generated_differential passes.
- cargo fmt and cargo test pass.
close_reason: Implemented switch lowering in src/lower.rs with labeled dispatch-loop fallthrough semantics, switch break handling, and loop continue interaction. Added differential fixtures for default, no-default, sparse, fallthrough, multiple labels, and switch-in-loop control. Updated c.bnf, docs/README.md, and cgen switch fuzzing. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo test after merge.

title: Implement C goto lowering
description:
Why: C goto is currently unsupported even though ClangIR emits explicit cir.goto/cir.label/cir.br control-flow for it. translate also fails before lowering on successor lists such as [^bb2], so Slate cannot handle goto fixtures today.

What to do:
- Extend the CIR parser/model to preserve MLIR successor lists on ops, at least for cir.br()[^bbN].
- Add baseline lowering for unstructured control flow involving cir.goto, cir.label, and cir.br.
- Use a conservative Rust dispatch-loop/state-machine representation for functions containing unstructured jumps, while preserving existing structured lowering for functions that do not need it.
- Add differential fixtures covering forward goto over dead code, backward goto loop, and goto nested inside if/scope.
- Update docs/README.md and c.bnf if goto becomes part of the supported subset.

Notes:
Observed CIR shapes:
- forward goto emits cir.goto <{label = "L"}> followed by separate ^bb blocks, cir.br()[^bbN], and cir.label <{label = "L"}> at the target block.
- backward goto inside if emits cir.goto inside cir.if, targeting a prior cir.label block.
Current parser error examples: expected '(' / unexpected ':' when it reaches successor lists or block labels after goto-generated blocks.
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo run -- translate succeeds for goto fixtures that currently fail to parse.
- generated Rust compiles and differentially matches C for forward goto, backward goto loop, and goto inside if/scope.
- existing structured-control fixtures still pass without unnecessary dispatch-loop lowering.
- cargo fmt and cargo test pass.
close_reason: Implemented C goto lowering: CIR parser now preserves MLIR successor lists ([^bbN]) and skips // predecessor comments on multi-block functions; functions with unstructured control flow (cir.goto/cir.label/cir.br across >1 block) lower to a state-machine dispatch loop with hoisted allocas, while structured functions keep the existing path. Added forward/backward/nested-in-if goto fixtures, a parser unit test, and docs/c.bnf coverage. Verified cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release (106 passed).

title: Fix long double extern return ABI for strtold
description: The stdlib/strtold probe translates and builds, but generated Rust receives -nan while C prints 2.75. The current LongDouble(f64) placeholder is not ABI-compatible for extern functions returning C long double on this target. Fix long double extern call/return representation so strtold and similar libc APIs differentially match C.
acceptance_criteria: tests/stdlib/stdlib/strtold.c is removed from KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED and cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture passes with the probe promoted.
close_reason: Implemented long-double ABI shims for strtold return storage and printf %Lf forwarding in generated calls; stdlib/strtold promoted from KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture, cargo test, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Lower main argc/argv parameters
description: Programs with int main(int argc, char **argv) currently generate fn main() but still assign argc = arg0 / argv = arg1, leaving undefined Rust identifiers. Add source/harness-aware lowering for main parameters, probably by collecting std::env::args into C-compatible argc/argv storage before lowering the body.
acceptance_criteria: A stdlib or misc probe using argv with a .args sidecar translates, compiles, and differentially matches C.
close_reason: Lowered int main(int argc, char **argv) by synthesizing C-compatible argc/argv bindings from std::env::args() in generated Rust main, keeping CString storage and a null-terminated argv pointer array alive for the function body. Added misc/argv.c plus .args sidecar. Verified with cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture (73 passed, 0 failed), cargo test, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Track stdlib probe failures as focused fix beads
description: When a new header probe fails, create a focused bead named for the exact missing CIR/lowering/runtime feature, temporarily list the probe in KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED with that bead id, then fix one bead at a time and promote the probe.
acceptance_criteria: The stdlib expansion workflow preserves the ratchet: every failing probe has a bead id in KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED, and every fix removes the entry.
close_reason: Implemented structured KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED entries with required bead IDs and metadata validation in tests/stdlib_coverage.rs. Verified with cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture and cargo test.

title: Create actual user C program corpus harness
description: After stdlib header coverage is broader, add a corpus area for small real-world C programs and libraries: compile original C and generated Rust, compare behavior, and record unsupported features as beads. Start with self-contained single-file programs before multi-file builds.
acceptance_criteria: A corpus harness exists with at least several real user-style C programs, and failures create focused beads instead of silently expanding unsupported surface.

title: Expand stdlib.h coverage
description: Add probes for common stdlib.h APIs: strtof/strtold/strtoll/strtoull with endptr, getenv with controlled env, atexit, abort/_Exit where harnessable, rand/srand deterministic sequence, aligned_alloc where available, realloc edge cases, bsearch/qsort variants, imaxabs/imaxdiv.
acceptance_criteria: New stdlib probes pass stdlib_coverage or each failure is isolated in a fix bead.
close_reason: Added stdlib probes for strtof/strtold/strtoll/strtoull endptr handling, rand/srand, aligned_alloc, atexit, and realloc edge cases. Fixed no-arrow CIR function-pointer type lowering so atexit callbacks compile. Filed slate-nk3.15 for the remaining strtold long-double extern ABI mismatch and listed stdlib/strtold in KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED. title: Lower void* casts/loads in comparator functions (qsort)

Generated Rust is 'let _v1: i32 = unsafe { *_v0 as *mut i32 };' which is nonsense (dereferences then casts i32 to a pointer). Need to model void pointers and pointer bitcasts + loads through them so *(const int*)a lowers correctly.
close_reason: Void* comparator casts are already implemented by commit 4676ac5: qsort lowers *(const int*)a as unsafe { *(_v0 as *mut i32) }, and stdlib qsort/bsearch pass. (Rust uses ! for integer bitwise NOT). Add a tests/fixtures/bitnot.c fixture and extend tests/support/cgen.rs + c.bnf to emit '~' on integer operands.

title: Support shift operators (cir.shift)
description: Lower the C '<<' and '>>' operators. Right shift is arithmetic vs logical based on operand signedness, which Rust's >> already matches by type, so no extra work is needed there. Add a cir.shift arm in lower.rs that reads the isShiftleft attribute and emits Rust << or >>, add tests/fixtures/shl.c and shr.c fixtures, and extend tests/support/cgen.rs + c.bnf to emit shifts. IMPORTANT for the generator: constrain shift amounts to [0, width) and avoid signed-overflow/negative-shift UB so C and Rust agree.
acceptance_criteria: cir.shift with isShiftleft lowers to <<, without to >>; shl.c and shr.c fixtures pass generated_differential; generator only emits well-defined shift amounts
close_reason: Implemented cir.shift lowering for left and right shifts with fixtures and generator constraints; committed before this session.
