title: Support simple printf width and flag forms for integers
description:
Why: formats like %04d, %-8d, %+d, and space-padded integers are common but require Rust format-string translation rather than a direct {} placeholder.

What to do:
- Parse a conservative subset of integer flags and static widths.
- Translate only forms with equivalent Rust formatting.
- Reject dynamic widths, precision, and combinations without a proven equivalent.
- Add unit tests for accepted and rejected forms.
close_reason: Implemented conservative static integer printf width/flag recovery for zero padding, left alignment, plus signs, and static widths; rejects dynamic widths, precision, space/# flags, and ambiguous combinations. Added unit tests plus printf_integer_widths differential fixture. Verified cargo fmt in the ticket worktree and cargo nextest r --release on main; main cargo fmt --check is currently blocked by unrelated dirty preprocessor edits.

title: Evaluate safe printf string and character macro recovery
description:
Why: %s and %c are common, but generated Rust often holds C pointers or integer character values, so blindly mapping them to Rust Display can change semantics.

What to do:
- Identify source/AST shapes where %c or %s can be translated exactly.
- Add AST support or helpers only if needed for safe rendering.
- Leave pointer strings and ambiguous character values on the libc path.
- Add fixtures covering both supported and rejected cases.
close_reason: Implemented conservative printf %s/%c macro recovery for direct constant UTF-8 C strings and constant ASCII character values, with local constant tracking and rejection of pointer strings, interior-NUL strings, and non-ASCII character bytes. Added unit tests plus supported/rejected differential fixtures. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release on main.

title: Rewrite heap alloc: malloc/calloc/realloc/free to Box/Vec
description:
On lifted owned heap regions (slate-58r.3):
- malloc(sizeof(T))/single-object -> Box<T> (or MaybeUninit init)
- malloc(n*sizeof(T))/calloc -> Vec<T> / vec![init; n]
- realloc -> Vec::resize/reserve
- free -> drop (RAII); explicit free removed

Correctness hinges entirely on the ownership analysis in slate-58r.3: only single-owner, non-escaping regions convert. calloc's zero-init and realloc's move/grow semantics must be preserved.
acceptance_criteria: - Single-owner allocations render as Box/Vec with free replaced by scope-drop; calloc zeroes, realloc grows correctly.\n- Escaping/aliased/custom-allocator regions stay raw libc.\n- Differential fixtures cover alloc-fill-free and realloc-grow.
notes: touches: src/fixups/rewrite/heap_ownership.rs, src/fixups/facts/mod.rs, tests/differential.rs, tests/fixtures/heap_*.c
close_reason: Rewrote owned malloc/calloc/realloc/free buffer patterns to Vec using heap ownership facts, with realloc resize/truncate and RAII drop. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Rewrite numeric parse: atoi/atol/strtol/strtoul/strtod
description:
On lifted &str (slate-58r.1): atoi/atol/strtol/strtoul/strtod -> str::parse::<T>().

Semantic gap to handle carefully: C atoi returns 0 on failure and parses a leading numeric prefix; strtol reports the end pointer and errno on overflow. Rust parse() is all-or-nothing and returns Result. Preserve C's leading-prefix + default-0 behavior (e.g. trim/prefix-scan then unwrap_or(0)); do not silently change overflow/failure semantics.
acceptance_criteria: - Parses render via str::parse with C-equivalent failure/prefix semantics (leading-numeric prefix, default 0 for ato*).\n- strtol end-pointer/errno consumers keep correct behavior or stay raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover valid, leading-prefix, empty, and overflow inputs.
close_reason: Implemented lifted atoi/atol/strtol/strtoul/strtod rewrites through generated __slate_runtime parse support, preserving endptr strtol calls as raw. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Rewrite sort/search: qsort/bsearch to sort_by/binary_search
description:
On lifted &mut [T]/&[T] (slate-58r.2):
- qsort(base,n,sz,cmp) -> slice.sort_by(|a,b| <cmp>) (or sort_unstable_by)
- bsearch(key,base,n,sz,cmp) -> slice.binary_search_by(...)

Requires lifting the C comparator function pointer into a Rust closure returning Ordering, and the (base,n,sz) triple into a typed slice (element size must match T). Non-matching element size or opaque comparators stay raw.
acceptance_criteria: - qsort/bsearch over lifted slices render as sort_by/binary_search_by with a comparator closure returning Ordering.\n- Element-size mismatch or opaque comparator stays raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover sort-then-search on ints and structs.
close_reason: Implemented qsort/bsearch slice idiomatization in src/fixups/rewrite/sort_search.rs with int and struct fixture coverage. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Rewrite string search: strchr/strrchr/strstr/strpbrk/strspn/strcspn
description:
On lifted &str/&[u8] (slate-58r.1):
- strchr(s,c) -> s.find(c) (mapped back to a pointer/offset per the return contract)
- strrchr -> s.rfind(c)
- strstr(s,sub) -> s.find(sub)
- strpbrk -> s.find(|ch| set.contains(ch)); strspn/strcspn -> position of first (non)member

Return-contract care: C returns a pointer into the buffer (or NULL); the lift must map the found index back to the original pointer/offset, mirroring the memchr rewrite (slate-58r / slate-04q.26).
acceptance_criteria: - Searches render as find/rfind/position over lifted operands; NULL/None and pointer-offset mapping preserved.\n- Unlifted operands stay raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover hit, miss, and last-occurrence cases.
close_reason: Implemented lifted strchr/strrchr/strstr/strpbrk/strspn/strcspn rewrites with ASCII-aware string facts and byte-search fallback. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Rewrite string copy/concat: strcpy/strncpy/strcat/strncat
description:
On lifted String/&str targets (slate-58r.1):
- strcpy(d,s)/strncpy -> d = s.to_owned() / d.clear(); d.push_str(s)
- strcat(d,s)/strncat -> d.push_str(s)

Ownership-sensitive: destination must be an owned String or a bounded buffer; capacity/truncation semantics of the n-variants must be preserved. Unlifted or fixed-capacity buffers stay raw.
acceptance_criteria: - Owned-target copies/concats render as to_owned/push_str; bounded n-variants preserve truncation.\n- Unlifted targets stay raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover copy, append, and truncating-n cases.
close_reason: Implemented a string_copy AST fixup for safe local char buffers, rewriting unused strcpy/strncpy/strcat/strncat to String to_owned/push_str forms with truncating n-variant coverage. Verified with cargo fmt && cargo nextest r --release.

title: Substrate: lift (T*, len) pointer+length pairs to &[T] / Vec<T>
description:
Analysis + lowering pass that recognizes a raw `T*` together with an element count as a Rust slice (`&[T]`/`&mut [T]`) or owned `Vec<T>`. The count is in ELEMENTS, not bytes -- must not confuse with byte lengths from mem*/size arguments.

Unlocks qsort/bsearch -> sort_by/binary_search and typed memcmp -> slice ==. Requires proving the length correctly bounds the allocation and the region has valid provenance; otherwise keep raw pointers.

## Context
Gates slate-58r sort/search and typed-compare rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: - Recognized (ptr, len) pairs lower to &[T]/&mut [T]/Vec<T> with element (not byte) length.\n- Slice bounds provably within the backing allocation; unprovable cases stay raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover array params passed with a length and in-place mutation.
close_reason: Implemented ptr_len AST fixup for exact full-array (T*, len) calls, rewriting function params to slices and callers to as_slice/as_mut_slice while leaving partial or unproved lengths raw. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Substrate: lift heap and resource handles (malloc/free, FILE*) to owned Rust types
description:
Ownership-analysis pass that maps C heap allocations (`malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc`/`free`) to `Box<T>`/`Vec<T>`, and resource handles (`FILE*` from `fopen`, and similar) to owned Rust types (`std::fs::File` + `io`). Hardest substrate: requires tracking ownership/lifetime, single-free, and error paths so the RAII drop matches C's explicit free/close.

Where ownership can't be established (escaping pointers, custom allocators, double-free-prone flows), leave the raw libc calls in place.

## Context
Gates slate-58r heap and stdio rewrites. Highest risk; ordered last among substrates.
acceptance_criteria: - Provably single-owner heap regions lower to Box/Vec with Drop replacing free; escaping/ambiguous ones stay raw.\n- FILE* handles with clear open/close scope lower to std::fs::File; leaks/aliased handles stay raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover alloc-use-free and open-read-close round trips.
close_reason: Implemented scalar heap ownership facts and rewrite for provably single-owner malloc/free flows to Box<T>, with shared-walker guidance in AGENTS/CLAUDE. Verified with cargo nextest r --release.

title: Idiomatize __slate_memchr scan loop into .iter().position() fixup
acceptance_criteria:
- The generated `__slate_memchr` uses `.iter().position()` over a `slice::from_raw_parts` slice instead of a manual while-index loop.
- Pointer-return contract is preserved exactly: a match maps the found index back to `bytes.add(i) as *mut c_void`, and not-found returns `std::ptr::null_mut()` (same base pointer arithmetic as today, so a hit returns a pointer into the original buffer, not the slice copy).
- Fixup operates on rust_ast nodes, never rendered strings; disabling it still yields correct Rust (correctness invariant per epic).
- Differential tests stay green; add/extend an output-shape assertion locking in the `.iter().position()` form for the memchr fixture.
notes: touches: src/lower.rs or src/fixups/rewrite/, src/rust_ast.rs/codegen.rs if match expression support is needed, tests/differential.rs, memchr/string fixtures
close_reason: Implemented memchr callsite lifting over iterable byte sources, NUL fast path from string facts, helper fallback/pruning. Verified with cargo nextest r --release.

title: Collapse declaration-initialized retval returns
description:
Why: generated helpers still emit patterns like 'let __retval: i32 = a & b; return __retval;' in bitand/div/mul/function_pointers and similar fixtures. This is correct but noisier than a direct return.

What to do:
- Add a fixup that recognizes a local __retval declaration with initializer immediately followed by 'return __retval'.
- Rewrite it to 'return <initializer>' and remove the declaration when __retval is not otherwise used.
- Keep multi-statement/multi-return retval cases on the baseline path.
- Preserve correctness if the initializer has side effects by only rewriting immediate declaration-return pairs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fixtures such as bitand.rs/function_pointers.rs no longer contain 'let __retval = ...; return __retval;' for simple helpers.
- Nontrivial retval control flow such as conditionals.classify remains unchanged unless separately proven.
- Differential tests stay green and output-shape coverage covers the direct return.
notes: touches: src/fixups/facts/control_flow.rs or retval facts, src/fixups/rewrite/retval.rs, tests around retval fixups/differential output
close_reason: Implemented a retval fact collector and rewrite consumer for declaration-initialized return slots, covering direct return output in function_pointers/cfg fixtures while preserving nontrivial uses. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Collapse final return-only temps
description:
Why: many generated functions end with an immediate temp round trip such as 'let _v11 = values[2]; return _v11;' or 'let _v6 = unsafe { *slot }; return _v6;'. This survives current pure-temp inlining because some expressions are deliberately not considered movable.

What to do:
- Add a conservative fixup for the exact adjacent pattern 'let temp = expr; return temp'.
- Rewrite to 'return expr' when the temp is synthetic, not otherwise used, and the declaration is immediately before the return.
- Treat volatile reads and unsafe dereferences carefully; immediate replacement is acceptable only if evaluation count/order is unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:
- arrays.rs, pointers.rs, volatile.rs, and function_pointers.rs lose simple final return temp declarations where safe.
- Used temps and non-adjacent temps remain materialized.
- Differential tests and focused output-shape assertions pass.
notes: touches: src/fixups/rewrite/, src/fixups/mod.rs, tests/differential.rs
close_reason: Implemented final_return_temps AST fixup after retval collapse, migrated legacy Item::Func to Item::Fn, and added output-shape coverage for arrays/pointers/volatile/function_pointers. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Collapse simple main zero-exit retval tail
description:
Why: many generated main functions still end with '__retval = 0; let _vN = __retval; std::process::exit(_vN as i32);' because the current main retval fixup only handles the smallest round trip. This appears in compound_assignments, chars, pointers, atomics, and many more fixtures.

What to do:
- Recognize a final main tail that stores a constant zero into __retval, loads it into a temp, and exits with that temp.
- Rewrite the tail to 'std::process::exit(0 as i32)' when __retval is not needed for any later observable behavior.
- Do not remove earlier __retval scaffolding in functions with early exits, dispatch state, or nonzero exit paths unless separately proven.

Acceptance criteria:
- Representative fixtures no longer emit a final '_vN = __retval; std::process::exit(_vN as i32)' for constant-zero main tails.
- Nonzero and control-flow-sensitive exit behavior is preserved.
- Differential tests stay green.
close_reason: Corrected main exit cleanup to elide only final zero std::process::exit calls in main and preserve nonzero/dynamic std::process::exit calls. Verified with cargo test main_zero_exit --bin slate, cargo test main_retval_boilerplate_is_collapsed --test differential -- --nocapture, cargo fmt, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Delete Expr::Raw: add Expr::Path, structure Val::Global/null_mut/fp/raw_expr producers

Add Stmt::While and Stmt::Block arms to substitute_in_stmt_structured so substitution is total, then delete substitute_in_stmt text fallback and the Stmt::Raw variant everywhere (rust_ast substitute_var, codegen render, fixups stmt_ident_count). Delete the dead Item::Raw text machinery (apply_text_fixups + eliminate_param_spills/collapse_retval/fuse_zero_init text passes + ~15 parse helpers); Item::Raw has zero producers so the text path is dead. The fn and its doc comment are now dead code in src/lower.rs. Remove them so Stmt::Raw is a true escape hatch with no normal emission path from lowering. title: Structure Item::Use path strings into a Path AST node
description:
Follow-up in the slate-737 raw-bridge cleanup. slate-737.6 introduced Item::Use/Item::Mod nodes, but their contents are still raw strings: Item::Use { path: String } is built with format!("crate::{module}::{name}") at src/lower.rs:281 and :306, and Item::Mod { name: String } holds a bare identifier.

title: Structuralize control-flow Stmt::Raw and remaining expr bridges
description:
Follow-up to the Rust-AST migration (slate-04q.13). Two bridge tiers remain:

(1) ~116 emit_line -> Stmt::Raw sites emit control-flow scaffolding (while/if/for/switch braces) as depth-annotated raw lines; the emitter reconstructs nesting from IndentStmt.depth. Model these structurally: Stmt::While and Stmt::Block already exist and are unused; add an If node (and For/Loop/Match as needed) and port lower_block/lower_if/lower_while/lower_for/lower_switch/lower_dispatch to build them instead of emit_line. This is the large, risky part -- do it incrementally, differential suite green at each step.

(2) ~24 materialize(String) + ~13 Val::expr sites still build format! strings for constructs without a modeled node (transmute, addr_of_mut!, array-literal .as_ptr(), struct field access, some pointer casts via render_pointer_operand). Add the missing Expr shapes (or accept Expr::Raw where genuinely one-off) and port.

Done in this pass (already merged): added Expr::MethodCall and Expr::Field; ported lower_overflow_arith (.0/.1), lower_ptr_diff (offset_from), lower_ptr_stride (offset), as_mut_ptr and long-double/bool cast conversions to structured nodes.

title: Emit Item::Fn directly; port remaining text fixups to AST passes
description:
Follow-up to slate-04q.13. The AST migration landed the structured Item::Fn body (typed Stmt::Let temps, Expr constructors, precedence-aware rendering) and moved the temp inliner onto the AST. But fixups::apply still renders Item::Fn to text and returns Item::Raw, so three passes remain text-based and emit() never consumes the structured Item::Fn at the end.

Remaining work:
- Port eliminate_param_spills, fuse_zero_init, collapse_retval from text (src/fixups/mod.rs) to AST passes over FnDef.body (Vec<IndentStmt>). They are currently insensitive to parenthesization (match idents/signatures), which is why they can still run on rendered text after the AST inliner — but they should operate on structured Stmt nodes.
- eliminate_param_spills also edits the FnDef.open signature line; keep that or model params structurally.
- Once all passes are AST-based, drop the render-to-text-then-Raw conversion in apply so Program::emit consumes Item::Fn directly as the final step.
- Consider whether Raw use-sites in the inliner (currently conservatively paren-wrapped via render_spliceable) can be reduced once assignments/returns become structured Stmt::Assign/Stmt::Return with real Expr targets — that would elide the remaining parens in 'a = (a - 5);' style output.

Verify: cargo nextest r --release green; cargo fmt.
close_reason: Implemented migrated function signatures as Rust AST data and ported parameter-spill elimination, zero-init fusion, and retval collapse to AST passes without converting Item::Fn back to text. Updated output-shape coverage for AST precedence rendering. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release on merged main.

title: Remove provably unnecessary parentheses in generated Rust
description:
rust_ast-level fixup that drops parentheses when Rust operator precedence and associativity make them provably redundant, so baseline lowering can keep emitting defensive parens for correctness while the fixup recovers idiom.

Baseline lowering wraps subexpressions in parens to preserve C evaluation order without reasoning about Rust precedence. Many are redundant once lowered (e.g. `(a * b) + c`, `return (x);`, `(a) + (b)`).

Scope: operate on the rust_ast, not text. Drop a paren group only when the parenthesized expression's precedence/associativity guarantees the same parse in its parent context; keep it otherwise. Must be precedence-correct across mixed arithmetic/bitwise/shift/comparison and unary contexts (Rust requires parens around some bitwise/comparison mixes — do not strip those).

Correctness invariant: this is an idiomatization fixup only. Disabling it must still yield correct Rust (extra parens are always safe). Pairs with slate-04q.7 (arg temp inlining) and slate-04q.11 (unnecessary mut removal), which also operate at the rust_ast layer.

Verify: differential tests stay green; add fixtures exercising nested arithmetic/bitwise/shift precedence and return-expr parens.
close_reason: Rendered control-flow conditions (if/let-if/match/expr-if/expr-match) bare instead of at PREC_CALL, matching Stmt::While; the precedence-aware renderer already emitted minimal arithmetic/bitwise/shift parens so no AST paren node existed to strip. Added redundant_parens.c fixture + assertion test.

title: Diagnose uncovered or unmapped preprocessor branches
description:
Why: Slate should not silently pretend to preserve portability when conditional C code was never observed or cannot be mapped to Rust cfgs. Unknown macro soup needs explicit user/build-system input.

What to do:
- Report conditional regions whose inactive branches were not covered by any configured variant.
- Report predicates that cannot be normalized to a Rust cfg or user-supplied feature mapping.
- Distinguish unsupported-but-recorded predicates from code shapes that cannot be merged cleanly.
- Include enough source location context for users to add config matrix entries.

Out of scope: guessing project macro semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
Uncovered branches in cfg fixtures or synthetic tests produce clear diagnostics.
Unknown project macros are reported with their predicate text and source location.
No guessed cfg attrs are emitted for unmapped predicates.
close_reason: Structured preprocess diagnostics distinguish unmapped-macro (unknown project macro, named + flagged uncovered when inactive) from opaque-predicate shapes; record-cfg emits {kind,line,message}; docs updated. Merged to main.

title: Document single-config versus portable multi-config translation
description:
Why: Slate currently translates the C program seen after preprocessing for one target/configuration. Multi-config cfg recovery changes the portability story and needs explicit user-facing documentation.

What to do:
- Document that single-config output is faithful to one preprocessed translation unit.
- Document the multi-config mode, built-in predicate mappings, user-supplied config matrix, and limitations.
- Explain why disabled code requires additional Clang/CIR invocations.
- Describe unsupported macro shapes and diagnostics.

Out of scope: promising full arbitrary macro-soup recovery.
acceptance_criteria:
Docs explain the semantic boundary between single-config and multi-config output.
Docs list the initial known mappings for _WIN32, __linux__, __APPLE__, x86_64, Arm/AArch64, and NDEBUG.
Docs explain how users should provide project-specific macro configurations.
close_reason: Added docs/cfg-portability.md: single-config vs multi-config semantics, the supported predicate->cfg table (_WIN32/__linux__/__APPLE__/x86_64/aarch64/arm/NDEBUG), user macro configs via SLATE_CLANG_ARGS + record-cfg, and refusal cases. Linked from CLAUDE.md and cfg fixtures README.

title: Remove provably unnecessary mut in generated bindings
description:
Why: several cleanup passes intentionally preserve mut for safety, especially parameter-spill fusion. After those rewrites, simple code like add.c can still contain mut bindings that are never assigned again. Removing unnecessary mut makes the output closer to idiomatic Rust and reduces warning suppression pressure.

What to do:
- Analyze generated Rust bindings after earlier mechanical cleanups.
- Remove mut from params and local lets when the binding is never assigned after initialization and is not borrowed mutably.
- Do not infer through raw pointers, address-taken locals, volatile accesses, or complex aliasing until those cases are modeled.
- Keep the pass as a cleanup only; it must not change generated behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
Simple add.c bindings that are never reassigned are emitted without mut after the relevant cleanup passes.
Bindings reassigned by translated C code remain mutable.
Address-taken or mutably borrowed bindings are left unchanged unless proven safe.
Differential tests stay green.
cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented remove_mut fixup over Rust AST bindings: removes mut from params/locals without later mutation, preserves mut for assignments, address-taking, mutable borrows, array mutable pointers, atomics, and method receivers. Added unit and differential shape coverage. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, stdlib_coverage, generated_differential, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Inline argument temps into type-safe call positions (rust_ast)
description:
Why: Baseline lowering materializes every call argument as its own let temp (e.g. `let _v1: i32 = 2; let _v3 = add(_v1, _v2);` then `printf(..., _v3)`). The existing pure-temp inliner (slate-04q.2) deliberately refuses call-argument positions because inlining a typed literal into a vararg slot loses its type (e.g. printf(_v0) with _v0: i64 = 9223372036854775807 must not become printf(9223372036854775807) — the literal would default to i32). Fixing this cleanly requires knowing callee signatures and preserving types, so this fixup should operate on the rust_ast, not on line-based text.

What to do:
- Move this fixup onto structured rust_ast nodes so callee signatures and argument types are available (per user direction: keep type information on the AST rather than a string side-table). The lowerer already emits every function signature; expose param types and the is_vararg flag to the fixup layer.
- Inline a single-use temp into a call-argument position when EITHER:
  (a) the callee is non-vararg and the target arg slot has a known param type (the param type pins any literal), OR
  (b) the temp initializer is itself a call (its return type is fixed by the callee signature, safe even in a vararg slot).
- Keep the existing hazard blocked: bare typed literals must NOT be inlined into vararg positions.
- For case (b) (impure call-result temp), require the def and use to be adjacent or separated only by pure temp-lets so no side effects are reordered.

Scope: only the two safe cases above. Do NOT emit `expr as T` casts to force a literal into a vararg slot — printf(2 as i32) is no cleaner than the temp and muddies the rule.

## Context
Second of two fixups from add.c review. User direction: handle on the rust_ast to keep type information (not a string side-table on the existing line rewriter). This is the "nontrivial fixup" the epic flagged as belonging on structured nodes. Depends on the parameter-spill fixup (slate-04q.6) landing first.
acceptance_criteria:
add.c call arguments inline to clean forms: add(2, 3) / add(-10, 4) / add(0, 0), and printf receives add(...) directly instead of a _vN temp.
Typed literals are still NOT inlined into vararg positions (existing regression tests stay green).
Impure call-result inlining never reorders side effects.
Differential tests stay green.
cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Added call_args rust_ast fixup: inlines single-use temps into (a) declared param slots of non-variadic callees and (b) call-result temps into any slot (incl. vararg) when no side effect sits between def and use. Vararg bare-literal hazard stays blocked. add.c now emits add(2,3)/add(-10,4)/add(0,0) with results handed directly to printf. 4 unit tests + differential shape assertion; cargo fmt + nextest (141) green.

description:
Why: Calls such as printf are emitted as let _vN = unsafe { printf(...) }; even when the return value is unused. Keeping the side-effecting call but dropping the unused binding makes generated Rust much closer to the source.

Only call-bearing inits are touched; used results and pure unused temps are left alone. Unusedness checked per lexical scope incl. block tails. compound_assignments/add.c now emit 'unsafe { printf(...) };'. 4 unit tests + differential shape assertion; integrated with slate-04q.5 (retval sig change) at merge; cargo fmt + nextest (149) green.

title: Wrap union array/aggregate member element access in unsafe
description: Why: reading or writing an array element of a union member (e.g. 'union { int i; unsigned char bytes[4]; }; v.bytes[0]') lowers to 'v.bytes[(0) as usize]' without an unsafe block, which fails E0133 because union field access is unsafe in Rust. Scalar union member access is already wrapped via the member_ptr path, but the element_ptr load/store path (lower.rs) emits no unsafe wrapper. What: detect when an element/member place resolves through a union member and wrap the access in unsafe. See slate-fvm which broadened aggregate coverage but left this case out (union_init.c fixture uses only scalar members as a result).
close_reason: Implemented union member unsafe propagation in src/lower.rs and added union_array_member differential fixture. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release before and after merge.

Consuming varargs (this) is distinct from calling variadic externs like printf, which already works.

title: Expand stdlib probe coverage (math/stdio/stdlib gaps)

title: Lower signal disposition sentinels SIG_IGN/SIG_DFL/SIG_ERR

title: Trim WORKFLOW.md coordination guide
description: WORKFLOW.md is referenced from CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. Review it for overlap and reduce duplicated or verbose content while preserving the multi-agent coordination rules.
close_reason: Trimmed WORKFLOW.md to focus on multi-agent coordination and removed duplicated command prose. Verified with git diff --check.

title: Respect linkage when exporting cross-TU functions/globals as pub
description:
Why: translate-project currently emits every non-main function as 'pub fn' and every initialized global as 'pub static mut' (lower.rs, gated only on ProjectInfo.emit_pub). That is not linkage-accurate: a C file-scope 'static int x' / 'static void f()' has internal linkage and is private to its translation unit, but Slate exports it pub anyway. Today this is harmless (no sibling declares an internal-linkage symbol, so nothing imports it), but it leaks visibility and would misbehave if two units each defined a 'static' symbol of the same name that should stay distinct.

What to do:
- Read CIR linkage on cir.func / cir.global (internal vs external) and only emit 'pub' for external-linkage definitions; internal-linkage (C 'static') defs stay private (no 'pub').
- Correspondingly, do not enter internal-linkage symbols into the pass-1 defined/defined_globals maps, so a sibling never imports them.
- Add a fixture under tests/fixtures.multi exercising same-named 'static' symbols in two units plus an external shared one, proving they stay distinct and the external one still imports.

Acceptance:
- Internal-linkage (static) funcs/globals are NOT pub and NOT importable across modules.
- External-linkage symbols still export pub and import via 'use crate::<mod>::<sym>;'.
- Differential fixture passes; cargo fmt + cargo test pass.
design: CIR carries linkage on cir.func/cir.global (e.g. linkage=0 external vs internal, or sym_visibility=private). Determine the exact attr from emit-cir on a 'static' symbol, then gate emit_pub per-definition on it. Thread a small helper (linkage_is_external) rather than a bare emit_pub bool once per-symbol granularity is needed.
close_reason: Read CIR linkage on cir.func/cir.global; only external-linkage (linkage=0) defs emit pub and enter the pass-1 defined maps, so C statics stay module-private and unimportable. Added tests/fixtures.multi/static_linkage (same-named statics in two units + shared external). Verified: cargo fmt + cargo test (full suite green).

title: Add first idiomatic Rust cleanup pass
description:
Why: Baseline lowering intentionally emits temp-heavy, unsafe, libc-backed Rust. Once behavior is correct, Slate needs optional fixups such as printf-to-println, temp cleanup, and simple reference/slice recovery.

What to do:
- Start with a narrow, proven printf-family to print!/println! rewrite for constant supported format strings.
- Keep the fixup optional in spirit: baseline Rust must remain correct without it.
- Add tests that verify output equivalence and reject unsupported dynamic or complex formats.
- Use structured Rust nodes where practical instead of broad text rewrites.
acceptance_criteria:
- Constant simple printf formats are rewritten to Rust formatting macros.
- Unsupported formats stay on the libc path.
- Differential tests verify output does not change.
- cargo fmt and cargo test pass.
close_reason: Closed

- Differential fixtures cover at least puts and a small string-operation set.
- Unsupported varargs cases fail clearly or emit explicit diagnostics, not silent wrong Rust.
- Existing printf fixtures still pass.
- cargo fmt and cargo test pass.

Existing fixture/stdlib coverage already covers puts and string operations via stdio_file_*, string_libc_fixup, string_copy_fixup, and stdlib stdio/string probes. title: Improve target-complete scalar type modeling
description:
Why: Slate mostly relies on CIR-emitted widths and handles common integer spellings, but target-complete C needs __int128, enum width/signedness details, and sharper ABI-sensitive scalar modeling.

What to do:
- Add fixtures for __int128 where the CIR toolchain emits it, enum variables/parameters/returns, and target-sensitive sizeof/sign behavior.
- Extend AST/CIR type mapping to preserve signedness, width, and enum backing behavior.
- Gate target-specific expectations through SLATE_TARGET/SLATE_CLANG_ARGS where necessary.
- Document any intentionally unsupported target corners.
acceptance_criteria: - Differential fixtures cover enum-typed variables/params/returns and any implemented extended integer widths.\n- Type mapping is driven by CIR/AST facts rather than hard-coded source spellings where possible.\n- cargo fmt and cargo test pass on the default target.

title: Generalize long double libc ABI shims
description: The strtold fix added focused helpers for strtold returns and the stdlib/strtold printf %Lf shape. Broaden this into a systematic lowering path for libc functions that return or accept C long double by value, including printf format shapes beyond one long double plus int and math *l APIs where covered.
acceptance_criteria: Long-double extern/libc calls are routed through generated or runtime C ABI helpers by signature/format shape instead of one-off strtold handling; new probes cover at least one additional return and one additional argument shape.
notes: Observed while implementing slate-04q.27.4: a direct fixture with long double x = 1.25L; printf("%Lf\n", x); stayed on libc printf as intended but produced Rust stdout 'nan' versus C '1.250000'. This is a baseline long-double varargs ABI issue, not a printf macro recovery case.

title: Expand constant/type header coverage
description: Add probes for float.h, limits.h, stddef.h, stdint.h, inttypes.h, stdalign.h, stdnoreturn.h, and stdbool.h constants/types/macros that real programs commonly use: FLT/DBL constants, offsetof, ptrdiff_t, intptr_t/uintptr_t, PRI*/SCN* macros, alignof/alignment macros.
acceptance_criteria: Constant/type header probes pass and document any missing parser/lowering support such as offsetof or format macro expansion.
close_reason: Added 12 constant/type header probes (float/limits/stdint/stddef/inttypes/stdalign). 11 pass incl. offsetof, PRI* macros, alignof, fixed-width types. stddef/ptrdiff exposed an address-of-array-element lowering gap, filed as slate-4n0 and ratcheted via KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED. Verified: cargo test.

title: Add locale.h coverage
description: Add C-locale probes for setlocale and localeconv, then cover locale-sensitive functions only under explicitly controlled locale settings.
acceptance_criteria: locale probes do not depend on host-specific installed locales beyond C/POSIX.
close_reason: Added C-locale probes; setlocale passes, localeconv tracked under slate-nk3.16 for struct lconv.

title: Add wchar.h and wctype.h smoke coverage
description: Add smoke probes for common wide-character and multibyte APIs: wcslen/wcscmp/wcschr, mbstowcs/wcstombs, mbrtowc/wcrtomb where deterministic, and basic wctype classifiers under C locale.
acceptance_criteria: Wide/multibyte probes either pass or produce focused beads for wchar_t, wide string literal, and mbstate_t support gaps.
close_reason: Added wchar/wctype smoke probes; wcscmp/wcschr/mbstowcs/iswctype pass, wcslen (wide literal as pointer) tracked under slate-nk3.17.

title: Complete ctype.h edge-case coverage
description: Add probes for remaining ctype.h classifiers and conversions: isblank, iscntrl, isgraph, isprint, isxdigit, EOF handling, unsigned-char boundary values, and locale-stable ASCII cases.
acceptance_criteria: ctype probes cover true/false/EOF/boundary cases and pass under the default C locale.

title: Add time.h coverage
description: Add deterministic probes for time.h APIs that can be made stable: mktime with fixed tm, gmtime/localtime under controlled TZ if harness supports it, strftime, difftime, clock where output is normalized to a predicate rather than an exact value.
acceptance_criteria: time.h probes are deterministic in CI/local runs and expose required struct tm / pointer-return support.
close_reason: Added deterministic time.h probes (difftime, clock, time; gmtime/mktime/asctime/strftime tracked under slate-nk3.16 for struct tm support).

title: Expand stdlib coverage probes
description: Add deterministic C stdlib probe programs for additional realistic libc usage, then fix translator gaps exposed by those probes so stdlib_coverage remains fully green.
close_reason: Added 15 deterministic stdlib probes covering FILE tmpfile I/O, stderr, sscanf, mixed printf formats, bsearch, realloc, strtod endptr, memchr, frexp/modf, and long-long division/abs variants. Implemented CIR multi-result parsing/projection support, cir.modf lowering, pointer-to-pointer cast rendering through slot addresses, and pointer bool comparisons against null_mut. Verified with cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture (70 passed, 0 failed), cargo test, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Model errno (__errno_location) as a thread-local lvalue
description: misc/errno: 'errno = 0' expands (glibc) to '*__errno_location() = 0'; generated Rust has an undeclared __errno_location -> compile error. Once external function decls exist (slate-4t0), the call links, but errno's macro/lvalue semantics (assignable dereference of the returned pointer) should be verified as a distinct case.
acceptance_criteria: stdlib_coverage misc/errno translates, compiles, and matches C output '0'
close_reason: Resolved by slate-4t0's extern mechanism: __errno_location is declared extern "C" and 'errno = 0' lowers to '*__errno_location() = 0' (lvalue-through-deref works), read lowers to '*__errno_location()'. stdlib_coverage misc/errno passes (output '0'), promoted out of KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED.

title: Support struct-returning library functions and libc aggregate typedefs (div_t/ldiv_t)
description: stdlib/div uses div(17,5) returning div_t by value; generated Rust has 'cannot find type div_t' and an undeclared div(). Need to model library aggregate typedefs returned/passed by value (div_t, ldiv_t, and similar) alongside external function decls, respecting the C ABI for small-struct returns.
acceptance_criteria: stdlib_coverage stdlib/div translates, compiles, and matches C output '3 2'
close_reason: Implemented local repr(C) standard division result structs for CIR aliases div_t/ldiv_t/lldiv_t/imaxdiv_t in src/lower.rs, added aggregate defaults, and promoted stdlib/div out of KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED. Verified with cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture, cargo test, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Lower cir.abs (and related CIR builtin ops) for abs/labs
description: abs(-5)/labs(...) lower to a cir.abs CIR op which slate does not handle -> todo!("cir.abs") and broken output. Handle cir.abs (and audit sibling builtin ops clang emits inline: fabs may fold, min/max, bit builtins) by lowering to the equivalent Rust (i32::wrapping_abs / .abs()).
acceptance_criteria: stdlib_coverage stdlib/abs and stdlib/labs translate, compile, and match C
notes: Also blocks math/{ceil,fabs,floor,round,trunc}: these lower to CIR builtin ops cir.ceil/cir.fabs/cir.floor/cir.round/cir.trunc (todo! in lower.rs), same family as cir.abs. Handle them alongside abs/labs (map to f64::ceil/abs/floor/round/trunc). Tracked in stdlib_coverage KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED under slate-kaf.
close_reason: Implemented CIR builtin unary lowering in src/lower.rs for cir.abs plus cir.ceil/cir.fabs/cir.floor/cir.round/cir.trunc. Promoted stdlib abs/labs and math ceil/fabs/floor/round/trunc out of KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED. Verified with cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture, cargo test, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Derive Clone/Copy on emitted C structs and unions (value semantics)
description: C structs/unions are value types: assignment and pass-by-value copy them. Emitted #[repr(C)] structs derived nothing, so passing a struct by value and reusing it produced 'use of moved value' in Rust. Derive #[derive(Clone, Copy)] on all emitted records; every field type Slate emits (scalars, raw pointers, arrays-of-Copy, Option<fn>, LongDouble, nested records) is Copy, so the derive is always valid for the supported subset.
design: Add #[derive(Clone, Copy)] to both struct and union headers in lower_record. Unions derive Clone via Copy. Validated by tests/fixtures/long_double_struct.c which passes a struct by value and reuses it.
close_reason: Implemented in src/lower.rs: LongDouble newtype (repr(C,align(16))) for long double, raw-identifier escaping for Rust-keyword collisions, and Clone/Copy derive on emitted C records. Full suite green incl. fuzzer; new fixture long_double_struct.c.

title: Escape C identifiers that collide with Rust keywords via raw identifiers (r#)
description: C identifiers can be valid Rust keywords (box, match, type, fn, loop, ...), which currently emit as-is and produce uncompilable Rust. sanitize_ident should wrap keyword collisions as raw identifiers (r#box). Four keywords cannot be raw identifiers (crate, self, super, Self) and must be mangled another way (trailing underscore).
design: Single choke point: sanitize_ident. After char-sanitizing, if the result is in the raw-unavailable set (crate/self/Self/super) append '_'; else if it is any other Rust keyword, prefix 'r#'. Raw idents are valid in type/field/fn/local positions so one fix covers all emit sites. union is a contextual keyword Slate itself emits for C unions — leave it usable as a plain ident.
close_reason: Implemented in src/lower.rs: LongDouble newtype (repr(C,align(16))) for long double, raw-identifier escaping for Rust-keyword collisions, and Clone/Copy derive on emitted C records. Full suite green incl. fuzzer; new fixture long_double_struct.c.

title: Represent long double as repr(C, align(16)) LongDouble newtype (layout fix)
description: Baseline long double currently lowers to bare f64 (8/8 layout), which silently breaks struct field offsets, union/memcpy punning, and array element placement wherever a long double shares a layout — the x86-64 SysV ABI wants size 16 / align 16. Introduce a #[repr(C, align(16))] struct LongDouble(f64) newtype with Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Neg impls so arithmetic still delegates to f64 (precision-lossy, tier 1) while the in-memory size/alignment matches the ABI. This is the layout tier; bit-exact x87 soft-float and libc/varargs interop remain out of scope (see slate-c2r).
design: Tier 1 of the long double ladder: correct layout, f64-precision arithmetic. rust_type maps !cir.long_double<...> to LongDouble; lower_const wraps literals as LongDouble(x); lower_cast converts int/float<->LongDouble via .0 / constructor; default is LongDouble(0.0). Prelude struct emitted only when used.
notes: DONE fully, including the C-AST struct-field path: c_type_to_rust(Float{bits:80}) -> LongDouble, default_c_value -> LongDouble(0.0), rust_c_type sets the prelude flag. Verified by tests/fixtures/long_double_struct.c (long double as struct field). Layout size=16/align=16 matches C on x86-64.
close_reason: Implemented in src/lower.rs: LongDouble newtype (repr(C,align(16))) for long double, raw-identifier escaping for Rust-keyword collisions, and Clone/Copy derive on emitted C records. Full suite green incl. fuzzer; new fixture long_double_struct.c.

title: Support ABI-exact long double libc interop
description: Baseline long double arithmetic is translated as f64, which is sufficient for Slate's current differential fixtures but not ABI-exact for libc APIs, varargs, or %Lf printf/scanf paths. Add target-aware long double representation and call/varargs lowering for libc interop.
close_reason: Won't fix: ABI-exact long double varargs interop (%Lf) is unreachable in stable Rust — x86-64 SysV passes long double as class X87 on the stack, and Rust has no f80 type nor a way to classify a value as X87; LongDouble(f64) is a 16-byte INTEGER/MEMORY struct. Printing long double via %Lf is uncommon and the generator never exercises it (always truncates through %d). If needed later, the achievable path is format-in-Rust + %s rewrite (f64 precision), not varargs.

title: Support volatile on types beyond local int
description: <type> allows 'volatile int' but params, fields, return types, and globals cannot be volatile. Extend volatile qualification to all applicable type positions.
close_reason: Implemented volatile-qualified primitive scalar support beyond local int by stripping volatile in source type parsing while preserving CIR is_volatile lowering. Added volatile_qualified_types fixture covering params, fields, returns, and globals; updated generator, grammar, and docs. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Support type qualifiers const, restrict, _Atomic
description: Add C type qualifiers const, restrict, and _Atomic to the type surface. Only 'volatile int' is currently supported among qualifiers.
close_reason: Implemented type qualifier coverage for const, restrict, and _Atomic via AST type normalization, fixture coverage, fuzzer generation, grammar, and docs. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Support function pointer types
description: Add C function pointer types, mapped to Rust fn pointers / Option<fn>. Depends on general pointer support.
close_reason: Implemented C function pointer locals and parameters as nullable Rust fn pointers, including nested CIR function type parsing, indirect call lowering, source AST type modeling, fixture coverage, fuzzer generation, grammar, and docs. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Support long double
description: Add C long double floating type. Listed in docs 'Not handled yet'. Requires deciding a Rust representation since Rust has no native long double.
close_reason: Implemented baseline long double support by mapping ClangIR !cir.long_double<!cir.f80> and source long double to Rust f64, adding fixture coverage, fuzzer coverage, grammar, and docs. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo run -- emit-fixtures.

title: Best-effort lowering of __attribute__((visibility(...))) with diagnostic fallback for protected
description:
Why: __attribute__((visibility("default"|"hidden"|"protected"))) controls ELF symbol visibility for shared-library builds -- hidden symbols are not exported from the shared object, protected symbols cannot be overridden by earlier-loaded shared objects or the executable. CIR carries this directly as a global_visibility numeric attr, but Rust has no per-symbol visibility attribute (stable or nightly) equivalent to Clang's __attribute__((visibility(...))) or -fvisibility.

Investigation performed: tested rustc's -Z default-visibility=hidden/protected unstable compiler flag directly (rustc 1.99.0-nightly). Per the unstable book (rust/src/doc/unstable-book/src/compiler-flags/default-visibility.md), this flag: (1) is crate/target-wide only, not per-symbol -- cannot mix visibilities within one crate/TU the way C attribute((visibility(...))) can per-declaration; (2) only affects shared-object builds, explicitly documented as having no effect on executables; (3) empirically confirmed to have NO EFFECT on #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn symbols even when building a cdylib -- readelf -sW showed GLOBAL DEFAULT for foo/bar under both -Z default-visibility=hidden and =protected, unchanged from the no-flag baseline. No further nightly attribute (#[rustc_visibility] or similar) was found in the rustc source tree search. Conclusion: there is no usable per-symbol Rust mechanism today for hidden/protected visibility on explicitly-exported FFI symbols -- this must be a diagnose-and-fallback feature, not a full lowering.

What to do:
- Read global_visibility from CIR (confirmed numeric encoding matches LLVM GlobalValue::VisibilityTypes: Default=0, Hidden=1, Protected=2) -- no AST JSON needed for detection.
- default (0): no special handling, proceed with normal emit_pub/no_mangle lowering from the other jep.4 tickets.
- hidden (1): closest faithful approximation is to NOT export the symbol at all (keep Rust-private, no #[unsafe(no_mangle)], no pub) since hidden C symbols are, by definition, invisible outside the linkage unit anyway -- document this as an intentional approximation (a hidden-but-still-directly-called-within-the-same-TU C function remains correctly callable since Slate lowers whole translation units together; only cross-shared-object visibility semantics are unrepresentable and moot for single-crate output).
- protected (2): no faithful Rust representation exists (see investigation above); diagnose as unsupported via diagnostics.warn(...) and fall back to default/exported behavior, following the existing jep.1/jep.3 diagnose-and-fallback precedent.
- Revisit this ticket if a future stable/nightly Rust per-symbol visibility attribute lands (tracking issue https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/131090 covers the crate-wide flag only, not a per-symbol attribute, as of this investigation).
design: CIR global_visibility attr numeric encoding confirmed via CIR dump: Default=0, Hidden=1, Protected=2, matching LLVM GlobalValue::VisibilityTypes. The crate-wide -Z default-visibility flag was investigated and ruled out as a per-symbol mechanism -- empirically confirmed no effect on individually no_mangle'd cdylib exports on the local nightly toolchain. This is the lowest-fidelity sub-ticket of jep.4 by necessity of Rust's current attribute surface, hence P4.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture: default-visibility C symbol lowers normally (no behavior change from the no_mangle ticket). Hidden-visibility C symbol lowers to a private (non-exported) Rust item with a passing differential test confirming in-TU behavior is unaffected. Protected-visibility C symbol produces a diagnostics.warn(...) and falls back to default/exported lowering rather than panicking or emitting incorrect Rust. cargo fmt/cargo nextest r --release green.
close_reason: Implemented hidden visibility as private/non-exported lowering, warned and fell back for protected visibility, documented the tradeoff, and verified with cargo fmt plus cargo nextest r --release.

title: Lower diagnostic and optimization attributes where Rust has direct equivalents
description:
Why: some attributes have straightforward Rust equivalents or useful analysis facts, but they are lower priority because they do not usually affect runtime correctness.

What to do:
- Evaluate deprecated, warn_unused_result, always_inline, noinline, cold, pure, const, format, sentinel, hot, and no_sanitize.
- Directly lower only attributes with clear Rust equivalents, such as deprecated, must_use, inline(always), inline(never), and cold.
- Treat pure/const/format/sentinel as analysis or diagnostics facts unless a semantic lowering is needed.

Acceptance: fixtures or unit tests cover directly lowered attributes and ignored/fact-only attributes; docs explain which attributes are semantic, diagnostic, optimization-only, or unsupported.

title: Evaluate compile-time selection builtins for source-level lowering
description:
Why: __builtin_choose_expr, __builtin_types_compatible_p, and related compile-time builtins are common in macro-heavy C. They may be folded away before CIR, but when source facts matter Slate should know whether there is anything to lower or document as pre-CIR-only.

What to do:
- Add small fixtures using macro-style compile-time selection builtins.
- Inspect CIR and Clang AST JSON to see whether selected values are already folded.
- If no runtime lowering is needed, document the behavior and add regression coverage.
- If an unfurled shape reaches Slate, add conservative source-fact lowering.

Assumption: these are compile-time constructs; Slate should not emulate a type system query at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures document whether the builtins disappear before CIR or require handling; any required handling has tests; docs describe the boundary so future macro-heavy failures are triaged correctly.

title: Document structured goto lowering boundary
description:
Why: future goto improvements should extend the CFG structurer rather than adding source-pattern one-offs or relying on fixups to reverse-engineer the dispatch state machine.

What to do:
- Document the lowering order: structured CFG recovery first, dispatch fallback second, Rust fixups afterward.
- Describe the first supported CFG shapes and rejection rules.
- Point to tests that distinguish structured and fallback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: - docs/architecture.md, docs/passes.md, or docs/idiomatization.md explains the goto lowering boundary.\n- The docs state that dispatch remains the correctness fallback.

title: Recognize simple slice reduction idioms
description: After loop recovery over lifted slices, optionally recognize simple reductions such as sum, product, bitwise and/or/xor accumulation, and possibly bitcount-like patterns. This is lower priority because explicit loops are already readable and Rust builtins/iterator adapters are more idiomatic only for narrow shapes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Simple accumulator loops over lifted slices can render as iterator reductions such as sum() when type inference and overflow semantics are safe.
- Bitwise reductions are considered only for exact, obvious accumulator patterns.
- Ambiguous overflow, side effects, early exits, or accumulator reuse leave the explicit loop intact.
- Output-shape tests cover at least one accepted reduction and one rejected near miss.

title: End-to-end fixtures and differential tests for value-macro selection
description: Adds fixtures and differential coverage per docs/macro-selection-interface.md. C sources using integer/char value predicates plus a slate-macros.toml; assert the generated crate compiles under each class feature and that C and Rust agree (differential) for each declared value. Include a rejection fixture (out-of-range value, cross-macro operand) asserting the diagnostics.
design: Depends on crate emission. Mirrors tests/fixtures.cfg and tests/cfg_translate.rs patterns. See docs/macro-selection-interface.md.
acceptance_criteria: A value-predicate fixture translates to a crate whose per-feature builds run identically to the C compiled with the matching -D<NAME>=<val>; out-of-range and cross-macro cases produce the documented diagnostics.
close_reason: Closed

title: Emit a buildable crate: Cargo.toml features, mutual-exclusion guard, --out
description: Implements crate emission per docs/macro-selection-interface.md (Generated features / Mutual exclusion / CLI). Add --out <dir> to translate-cfg: render Cargo.toml with [features] (one per class + a default from each macro's declared default), the merged src/, and a compile-time mutual-exclusion guard (compile_error! for zero or >1 selected class features per macro). cargo build with no flags must match one real configuration.
design: Depends on planning/pinning/merge and cfg synthesis. Cargo features are additive, so exclusivity is enforced via compile_error!. See docs/macro-selection-interface.md.
acceptance_criteria: --out writes a crate that cargo builds under the default features and under an explicit --features selection; selecting two class features of one macro, or none, fails at compile time with a clear message; default feature matches the declared default value.
close_reason: Closed

title: Plan and pin value-macro configs and merge variants
description: Threads the TOML through translate-cfg and extends plan_configs/pin_args per docs/macro-selection-interface.md (CLI + Implementation notes). Add --macros <file> to translate-cfg. For each surviving class of each declared macro, add -D<NAME>=<repr-value> to the Clang/CIR invocation (as pin_args already pins defined() atoms), run the matrix, reuse merge_variants unchanged — identical items collapse, differing items gate behind the class feature. Independent regions do not multiply.
design: Depends on class computation and cfg synthesis. Reuses merge_variants. See docs/macro-selection-interface.md (CLI: generating a crate).
acceptance_criteria: translate-cfg --macros produces per-class variants pinned with -D<NAME>=<val>; merged output gates differing items behind class-feature cfgs; classes join the existing target/debug matrix without cross-product blowup for independent regions.
close_reason: Closed

title: Synthesize cfgs from Compare via the class table (pred_to_cfg Compare arm)
description: Adds a Compare arm to pred_to_cfg per docs/macro-selection-interface.md (Generated features and lowering). Using the class table as context, lower a comparison to cfg over the class features whose class satisfies it (evaluate at a class representative), e.g. LOG>=3 -> cfg(feature=log_1000000). Boolean ops compose as all/any/not; cross-macro single-macro-vs-constant atoms compose too.
design: Depends on class computation. pred_to_cfg becomes context-carrying (needs the class table), unlike today's context-free mapping. See docs/macro-selection-interface.md.
acceptance_criteria: Compare predicates lower to the correct any()/all() over class features; boolean combinations compose; mapping matches the class partition; existing defined()-based cfg mapping unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Compute value classes: predicate partition + build-set intersection + feature names
description: Pure module implementing the reduction in docs/macro-selection-interface.md (The reduction). Per declared macro: collect every constant in Compare predicates (including ==/!= targets for soundness), sort into breakpoints, build the equivalence-class partition, intersect with the declared build value set, and assign one deterministic feature name per surviving class (by class-min). No Clang; heavily unit-testable.
design: Depends on TOML loader and Compare grammar. See docs/macro-selection-interface.md (The reduction, soundness rule). Class table feeds cfg synthesis and config planning.
acceptance_criteria: Given predicates and a declared value set, produces the minimal class partition (bounded by code, not domain); values indistinguishable by any predicate share a class; only classes containing a declared value survive; feature names deterministic. Covers the worked LOG example (>=3,==1,<5 with {1,1000000} -> 2 features).
close_reason: Closed

title: Parse value comparisons (macro op int) as PredExpr::Compare
description: Extends the preprocess.rs predicate grammar per docs/macro-selection-interface.md (Implementation notes). Recognize <macro> <cmp> <int-const> (and reversed), cmp in ==,!=,<,<=,>,>=, character constants as integers, producing PredExpr::Compare { macro, op, value } — ONLY when the macro is declared in the TOML; undeclared macros stay PredExpr::Opaque so they still refuse. Boolean &&/||/! over Compare atoms compose as today.
design: Depends on the declared-macro set from the TOML loader. New PredExpr variant; keep opaque fallback intact. See docs/macro-selection-interface.md.
acceptance_criteria: Comparisons on declared macros parse to Compare; comparisons on undeclared macros remain opaque-predicate naming the macro; char constants parse as integers; boolean combinations of Compare atoms are recorded.
close_reason: Closed

title: Parse slate-macros.toml and validate values against declared type
description: Implements the TOML interface and type validation from docs/macro-selection-interface.md. Load [macros.<NAME>] entries with type (required C integer type), values or range, and optional default. Resolve each type to [min,max] against the active target (SLATE_TARGET) — char signedness and widths included — and reject any declared value or range bound outside it with a hard error naming the macro, type, and offending value (type=char + 256 is denied). Pure, no Clang; unit-testable.
design: Foundational for the value-matrix work; see docs/macro-selection-interface.md (TOML interface + Types and validation). Provides the declared-macro set later stages key on.
acceptance_criteria: Valid TOML parses into a per-macro model (type, value set, default); out-of-range values and non-integer literals are rejected pre-Clang with a macro/type/value error; char/width ranges resolve against SLATE_TARGET.
close_reason: Closed

title: Value-carrying preprocessor predicates: rationale and bounded user-matrix path
description:
Why: numeric/value predicates like #if FOO == 2, #if FOO > 3, #if __GNUC__ >= 9 are refused (opaque-predicate) by translate-cfg. Root cause: Rust cfg / Cargo features are a BOOLEAN PRESENCE model — a feature is on or off and carries no value — so there is no cfg form for 'FOO's value >= 3'. This ticket captures the rationale and the only bounded, non-guessing path forward, distinct from the plain #ifdef work in slate-rs5.

Why it's hard (not just unimplemented):
- No direct mapping: cfg(feature=..) can't express a numeric comparison.
- Emulation requires enumerating the macro's VALUE DOMAIN into mutually-exclusive flags: FOO==2 -> cfg(feature="foo_2"); FOO>=2 -> cfg(any(feature="foo_2", feature="foo_3", ...)). C never states the domain, so inventing it is guessing project semantics (forbidden) and unbounded.
- Runtime lowering (const + if) does NOT rescue whole-item gating: both branches may define the same symbol differently, and two fn foo cannot coexist at runtime the way two #[cfg]-gated defs can.

Two sub-cases with different ceilings:
- Toolchain-fixed macros (__GNUC__, __STDC_VERSION__, _MSC_VER): value is concrete at translate time so the predicate is decidable, but Rust has NO compiler/language-version cfg, so there is no portable target — genuine dead end for portable recovery (only option is baking in the current toolchain's branch, which is unfaithful).
- Build-supplied value macros (-DVERSION=3): salvageable ONLY with a user-supplied value matrix -> mutually-exclusive feature encoding, with comparisons lowered to any()/all() over the enumerated set.

What to do:
- Document the boolean-presence limitation and these two sub-cases in docs/cfg-portability.md (why value predicates are refused).
- Design (not necessarily build) the user-supplied value-matrix interface: user declares FOO in {1,2,3}; Slate emits mutually-exclusive features and lowers ==, <, <=, >, >=, != to any()/all() over that domain, and enforces exactly-one-selected.
- Keep automatic (no-matrix) handling refusing with the opaque-predicate diagnostic.

Out of scope: guessing value domains automatically; compiler/language-version portability (no Rust cfg exists).
design: Successor under slate-mt9; the value-predicate counterpart to slate-rs5's boolean #ifdef work. Comparison lowering is any()/all() over an enumerated, user-declared domain with an exactly-one-of constraint. Toolchain-fixed version macros are explicitly not portably recoverable.
acceptance_criteria: Docs explain why value predicates are refused (boolean-presence cfg model) and the toolchain-fixed vs build-supplied split; a design exists for a user-supplied value matrix that lowers numeric comparisons to mutually-exclusive feature cfgs; without a matrix, value predicates still refuse via opaque-predicate diagnostics.
notes:
Value-matrix design (agreed spec):

Interface: user declares a per-macro BUILD VALUE SET (the values they actually compile with), e.g. LOG in {1, 1000000}. User declares VALUES, never features — Slate derives feature names and cfgs itself, best-effort.

Reduction (two composing passes):
1. Predicate partition: collect all distinct constants any comparison uses on the macro; sort into breakpoints; the value line splits into equivalence classes (each exact constant + open intervals between, clamped to domain) where every predicate has constant truth. Class count bounded by the CODE (<= 2k+1 for k constants), not the domain. Soundness rule: derive breakpoints from EVERY constant including == / != targets, so two values merge only when no predicate distinguishes them (then output is provably identical).
2. Build-set intersection: keep only classes containing a declared build value. Final feature cardinality <= number of declared values. This is the LOG in 1..1M -> 2 features collapse (e.g. {1}->A, {1000000}->D).

Lowering: emit one Cargo feature per surviving class, with an exactly-one-of constraint; each comparison -> cfg(any/all(...)) over the class features whose class satisfies it; &&/||/! compose as all/any/not.

In scope: each macro compared only to constants; boolean combinations of such comparisons, even across macros (LOG==2 && METRIC==3 -> all(feature=log_c2, feature=metric_c3)) since each atom is still single-macro-vs-constant.

Out of scope (refuse via opaque-predicate): CROSS-MACRO operands where a single comparison mixes two macros (LOG > METRIC, LOG + METRIC > 5) — needs the cartesian product of class sets, re-expanding cardinality. Decision: NO cross-macro combination declarations; one set per macro only. Affine arithmetic on a single macro (LOG*2 > 10 -> LOG > 5) is a possible later fold, not part of this.
close_reason: Closed

title: Support additional printf integer length modifiers
description: Why: %hd, %hhd, %jd, and %td are common length variants whose printed value can often use the same Rust display formatting after CIR lowering. What: evaluate and recover these length modifiers for already-supported integer conversion kinds while rejecting cases where argument lowering or signedness is ambiguous. Acceptance: fixtures cover short, signed char, intmax, and ptrdiff style inputs where CIR produces stable argument shapes.

title: Evaluate printf scientific and general float conversions
description: Why: %e, %E, %g, and %G appear in numeric C output, but exact formatting semantics can differ. What: compare C and Rust behavior, implement only demonstrably compatible static cases, and file narrower follow-ups if exact parity needs helpers. Acceptance: differential fixtures document supported cases or record why the conversion remains unsupported.

title: Support printf character width forms
description: Why: %3c and %-3c are simple extensions of existing conservative %c support. What: recover static width and left alignment for character conversions when the character argument is already safely recoverable, and reject unsupported dynamic width or ambiguous character values. Acceptance: parser tests and fixtures cover right and left aligned characters.

title: Rewrite stdio: fopen/fread/fwrite/fgets/fputs/fclose to std::fs + io
description:
On lifted FILE* handles (slate-58r.3):
- fopen -> std::fs::File::open/create (mode string -> OpenOptions)
- fread/fwrite -> Read::read/Write::write on the file
- fgets/fputs -> BufRead::read_line / write
- fclose -> drop (RAII)

Largest surface and lowest commonality in the current test corpus -> lowest priority. Buffering, error/errno, and EOF semantics must be preserved; stdin/stdout/stderr FILE* map to std::io::{stdin,stdout,stderr}.
acceptance_criteria: - File handles with clear open/close scope render as std::fs::File + io traits; fclose becomes scope-drop.\n- Mode-string -> OpenOptions mapping correct; EOF/short-read semantics preserved.\n- Differential fixtures cover write-then-read-back and line iteration.
close_reason: Implemented conservative stdio rewrite for literal fopen/fputs/fclose owners with OpenOptions and write_all, added stdio_file_write differential coverage, and filed follow-ups for close lifetime, fgets, and fread/fwrite. Verified before merge with cargo nextest r --release; post-merge test run was user-aborted as accepted.

title: Remove unnecessary unsafe around safe field reads
description:
Why: fixtures such as structs.rs and non_int_fields.rs emit 'unsafe { p.left }' for local struct field reads. Field access on safe local structs does not need unsafe, while union fields and static mut globals do.

What to do:
- Add a fixup or lowerer-side AST annotation that can distinguish safe struct field reads from union/static-mut field reads.
- Remove unsafe wrappers only for proven-safe local struct field accesses.
- Leave union field reads, static mut field reads, raw pointer derefs, and volatile accesses unsafe.

Acceptance criteria:
- structs.rs local Pair reads render as 'p.left'/'p.right' without unsafe.
- unions.rs and global_vars.rs keep required unsafe field/global access.
- Differential tests and output-shape assertions cover both removal and keep-safe cases.
notes: touches: src/fixups/, src/rust_ast.rs if needed, tests/differential.rs, tests/fixtures/structs.c, tests/fixtures/non_int_fields.c, tests/fixtures/unions.c, tests/fixtures/static_globals.c
close_reason: Implemented member-load lowering so safe local struct field reads use plain field access while union/static-mut/raw/volatile cases remain unsafe. Added differential output-shape coverage for structs, non_int_fields, unions, and global_vars. Verified after merge with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Simplify constant array index casts
description:
Why: array fixtures emit indexes like 'values[(0 as usize)]' and globals emit 'numbers[(2 as usize)]'. These casts are correct but noisy for literal nonnegative indexes.

What to do:
- Add an expression fixup that rewrites literal integer index casts to plain usize-compatible literals in indexing positions.
- Start with nonnegative integer literals only: '0 as usize' -> '0'.
- Leave dynamic casts like '((index as i64) as usize)' alone unless a separate proof is added.

Acceptance criteria:
- arrays.rs/array_types.rs no longer contain '(0 as usize)' style indexes for literal constants.
- Dynamic and potentially signed indexes remain unchanged.
- Differential tests stay green.
close_reason: Implemented AST fixup for nonnegative literal usize array indexes in src/fixups/rewrite/constant_index_casts.rs, with unit and differential shape coverage. Verified after merge with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Recover idiomatic pointer add/deref forms
description:
Why: pointer fixtures emit nested forms like 'unsafe { *unsafe { _v8.offset(_v9 as isize) } }' and copy fixtures embed 'unsafe { buf.as_mut_ptr().offset(...) }'. Rust exposes clearer raw-pointer APIs such as add/sub and can avoid nested unsafe blocks in some cases.

What to do:
- Analyze generated pointer arithmetic/deref AST shapes and choose a safer canonical spelling.
- Prefer nonnegative usize offsets with '.add(idx)' when the source index is known nonnegative; otherwise keep '.offset(...)'.
- Avoid changing aliasing, provenance, or signed-offset behavior.
- Collapse nested unsafe only when the inner/outer unsafe requirements are preserved.

Acceptance criteria:
- pointers.rs and mem_bcopy_overlap.rs have clearer pointer arithmetic spelling for proven-safe cases.
- Negative/signed offset cases remain baseline.
- Differential tests stay green with focused output-shape coverage.
close_reason: Implemented pointer stride cleanup in src/lower.rs: nonnegative constant and unsigned CIR pointer strides render with raw-pointer add, signed dynamic strides keep offset, nested unsafe deref wrappers are collapsed, and mem copy/set operands drop redundant inner unsafe under the outer unsafe operation. Added differential output-shape coverage for pointers.c and mem_bcopy_overlap.c. Verified after merge with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Remove redundant one-statement block scopes
description:
Why: generated code still contains C-shaped scopes that only wrap a single structured statement, e.g. '{ if n < 10 { ... } }' in conditionals.rs and function_prototypes.rs. These scopes no longer add readability once control flow is structured.

What to do:
- Add a fixup that unwraps Stmt::Scope bodies containing exactly one structured statement and no declarations whose lifetime must be preserved.
- Start with singleton scopes around If/Match/Loop statements where removing the braces cannot change name visibility.
- Leave scopes that contain local declarations plus later statements, labeled blocks, or dispatch state machines unchanged until proven.

Acceptance criteria:
- conditionals.rs and function_prototypes.rs lose redundant outer braces around singleton if statements.
- Scope-sensitive fixtures still compile and behave correctly.
- Differential tests stay green.
close_reason: Implemented singleton_scopes AST fixup for safe singleton If/Loop/Match scopes, registered it after return-temp cleanup, and added unit plus differential output-shape coverage for conditionals/function_prototypes. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Support setjmp/longjmp non-local control flow
description: tests/stdlib/setjmp/setjmp.c fails to build: the file-scope 'jmp_buf buf;' global is not emitted, the '__jmp_buf_tag' type is undefined, and setjmp's return-twice semantics have no direct Rust equivalent. Hard/rare; deprioritized. May need a runtime shim or intrinsic-style lowering.

title: Add signal.h and setjmp.h deterministic smoke coverage
description: Add minimal deterministic probes for signal.h and setjmp.h: raise with a simple handler where safe, signal disposition smoke tests, setjmp/longjmp control-flow smoke. Keep these small because they stress control flow and runtime behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Any signal/setjmp probes are deterministic and failures are split into focused control-flow/runtime beads.
close_reason: Added signal/setjmp smoke probes; raise+handler passes, SIG_IGN tracked under slate-nk3.18, setjmp/longjmp under slate-nk3.19.

title: Support _Complex / _Imaginary types
description: Add C complex/imaginary floating types (_Complex, _Imaginary). No native Rust equivalent; requires a struct-based representation.
close_reason: Complex support: fuzzer (cgen.rs) now emits double _Complex +/- with __real__/__imag__; c.bnf, docs/README.md, and docs/fuzzing.md document it. Fixed ca/cb name collision with char locals (renamed to cplxa/cplxb/cplxs). Full suite + fuzzer green.
